title.zh: 卷六十 列傳第五十 范岫 傅昭 孔休源 江革 徐勉 許懋 殷鈞
title.en: Volume 60 Biographies 50: Fan Xia, Fu Zhao, Kong Xiuyuan, Jiang Ge, Xu Mian, Xu Mao, Yin Jun
title.raw: 卷六十 列傳第五十 范岫 傅昭 孔休源 江革 徐勉 許懋 殷鈞 Volume 60 Biographies 50: Fan Xia, Fu Zhao, Kong Xiuyuan, Jiang Ge, Xu Mian, Xu Mao, Yin Jun

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十

translations.literal: Biographies, number fifty.
translations.idiomatic: the 50th year of Biographies

sentences.zh: 范岫傅昭孔休源江革徐勉許懋殷鈞

translations.literal: Fan Xia, Fu Zhao, Kong Xiuyuan, Jiang Ge, Xu Mian, Xu Mao, Yin Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xia, Fu Zhao, Kong Xiuyuan, Jiang Ge, Xu Mian, Xu Mao, and Yin Jun

sentences.zh: 高祖宣，晉徵士。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Xuan was a summoned scholar under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Xuan had been a summoned scholar under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父羲，宋尚書殿中郎，本州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Xi was Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat under Song and administrative aide in his home province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi served under Song as Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat and as administrative aide in his home province.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕反，羲在城中，事平遇誅。

translations.literal: When Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled, Xi was inside the city, and after the affair was settled he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled, Xi was inside the city; after the revolt was put down, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 岫幼而好學，早孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xia from youth loved learning; orphaned early; served his mother and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xia loved learning from childhood. Orphaned at an early age, he cared for his mother and became renowned for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 外祖顏延之早相題目，以為中外之寶。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Yan Yanzhi early marked him out and regarded him as a treasure within and without.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Yan Yanzhi singled him out early on, calling him a treasure to the family and to the world at large.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗臨荊州，引為主簿。

translations.literal: When Cai Xingzong came to Jingzhou, he recruited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Xingzong took charge of Jingzhou, he appointed Xia as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 及蔡將卒，以岫貧乏，遺旨賜錢二十萬，固辭拒之。

translations.literal: When Cai was about to die, because Xia was poor, he left instructions to grant him two hundred thousand in cash; Xia firmly declined and refused it.
translations.idiomatic: As Cai lay dying, knowing that Xia was poor, he left instructions to bequeath him two hundred thousand cash. Xia steadfastly refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為太子家令。

translations.literal: He served Qi as steward of the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi dynasty he served as steward of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子之在東宮，沈約之徒以文才見引，岫亦預焉。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhuì was in the Eastern Palace, Shen Yue and others were recruited for literary talent, and Xia also took part.
translations.idiomatic: While Crown Prince Wenhuì resided in the Eastern Palace, Shen Yue and others were brought in for their literary gifts, and Xia was among them.

sentences.zh: 岫文雖不逮約，而名行為時輩所與。

translations.literal: Xia's writing, though not equal to Yue's, was in conduct and reputation granted by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's prose did not match Yue's, but his reputation and conduct won the esteem of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 博涉多通，尤悉魏、晉以來吉凶故事。

translations.literal: Broadly versed and widely learned, he especially knew auspicious and inauspicious precedents from Wei and Jin onward.
translations.idiomatic: Widely read and deeply learned, he was especially versed in ritual and ceremonial precedents from the Wei and Jin dynasties onward.

sentences.zh: 約常稱曰：「范公好事該博，胡廣無以加。」

translations.literal: Yue often praised him, saying: "Master Fan is fond of affairs and thoroughly broad; Hu Guang cannot surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Yue often said of him, "Master Fan's enthusiasm for learning and breadth of knowledge are such that even Hu Guang could not surpass him."

sentences.zh: 南鄉範雲謂人曰：「諸君進止威儀，當問範長頭。」

translations.literal: Fan Yun of Nanxiang said to others: "Gentlemen, in your comings and goings and in ceremonial bearing, you should consult Long-Head Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun of Nanxiang told others, "When it comes to proper conduct and ceremonial bearing, you should consult Long-Head Fan."

sentences.zh: 以岫多識前代舊事也。

translations.literal: This was because Xia knew many old affairs of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: This was because Xia knew so many precedents and customs from earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 岫長七尺八寸，姿容奇偉。

translations.literal: Xia was seven feet eight inches tall, with a singular and imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Xia stood seven feet eight inches tall, with a striking and imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 永明中，魏使至，詔妙選朝士有辭辯者，接使於界首，故以岫兼淮陰長史迎焉。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, when a Wei envoy arrived, an edict finely selected court officials with eloquence to receive the envoy at the border; therefore Xia was appointed concurrently chief clerk of Huaiyin to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era, when an envoy from Wei arrived, the court was ordered to select the most eloquent officials to receive him at the border. Xia was therefore appointed concurrently chief clerk of Huaiyin to welcome the envoy.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and became Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning and observed it beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he entered mourning and observed the rites with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷頻起，並不拜。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly summoned him, but he did not accept any appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly summoned him to office, but he refused each time.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亮其哀款，得終喪制。

translations.literal: The court appreciated his sincere grief and allowed him to complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: The court respected the depth of his grief and permitted him to complete the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 出為安成內史，創立鈞折行倉，公私弘益。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Ancheng, established graded traveling granaries, and greatly benefited public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Ancheng, where he established tiered traveling granaries that greatly benefited both the government and the people.

sentences.zh: 征黃門侍郎，兼御史中丞，吏將送一無所納。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Censor-in-Chief; clerks and generals who presented gifts he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Censor-in-Chief. He accepted no gifts whatsoever from clerks or military officers who came to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 永元末，為輔國將軍、冠軍晉安王長史，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan, he was General Who Assists the State, chief clerk to Prince Jin'an of Champion, and acted in the affairs of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongyuan era, he served as General Who Assists the State and chief clerk to Prince Jin'an of Champion, administering the affairs of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝平建鄴，承制徵為尚書吏部郎，參大選。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang, by provisional order he was summoned as Director of the Personnel Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat and took part in the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Liang captured Jiankang, he was summoned by provisional order to serve as Director of the Personnel Bureau and to participate in the chief appointments of officials.

sentences.zh: 天監五年，為散騎常侍、光祿大夫，侍皇太子，給扶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianjian, he was Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attending the crown prince, with a staff granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianjian, he was appointed Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attending upon the crown prince with a walking staff provided for his use.

sentences.zh: 累遷祠部尚書，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Rites and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Minister of Rites and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 岫恭敬儼恪，進止以禮，自親喪後，蔬食布衣以終身。

translations.literal: Xia was reverent, dignified, and strict; in comings and goings he observed ritual. From his parents' mourning onward, he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth for life.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was reverent, dignified, and disciplined, conducting himself always according to proper ritual. After his parents' deaths, he ate only vegetables and wore plain cloth for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 每所居官，恒以廉潔著稱。

translations.literal: In every office he held, he was always renowned for integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held, he was known for his incorruptibility.

sentences.zh: 為長城令時，有梓材巾箱，至數十年，經貴遂不改易。

translations.literal: When he was magistrate of Changcheng, he had a catalpa-wood towel box; for several decades, even after he had become eminent, he did not replace it.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Changcheng, he used a catalpa-wood towel box that he kept for decades without replacing, even after he had risen to high rank.

sentences.zh: 在晉陵唯作牙管筆一雙，猶以為費。

translations.literal: At Jinling he made only one pair of bamboo-tube pens, and even that he considered extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: While at Jinling he used only a single pair of bamboo-tube pens, which he still regarded as an unnecessary expense.

sentences.zh: 所著文集、禮論、雜儀、字訓行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings, Ritual Discourses, Miscellaneous Ceremonies, and Character Instruction circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings, Ritual Discourses, Miscellaneous Ceremonies, and Character Instruction circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 二子褒、偉。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Bao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Bao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 傅昭字茂遠，北地靈州人，晉司隸校尉咸七世孫也。

translations.literal: Fu Zhao, styled Maoyuan, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi, seventh-generation descendant of Xian, Censor-in-Chief of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhao, styled Maoyuan, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi and a seventh-generation descendant of Xian, Censor-in-Chief under the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祖和之，父淡，善三禮，知名宋世。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Hezhi; his father Dan was skilled in the Three Rites and was renowned in the Song era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Hezhi, and his father Dan was an expert in the Three Rites who gained renown during the Song dynasty.

sentences.zh: 淡事宋竟陵王誕，誕反坐誅。

translations.literal: Dan served Prince Dan of Jingling of Song; when Dan rebelled he was executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Dan served Prince Dan of Jingling under the Song. When the prince rebelled, Dan was executed as an accomplice.

sentences.zh: 昭六歲而孤，哀毀如成人，為外祖所養。

translations.literal: Zhao was orphaned at six; his grief and emaciation were like an adult's, and he was raised by his maternal grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao lost his father at the age of six and mourned with the grief and self-denial of an adult. He was raised by his maternal grandfather.

sentences.zh: 十歲，於朱雀航賣曆日，雍州刺史袁顗見而奇之。

translations.literal: At ten, at Zhuque Crossing he sold calendar almanacs; Yuan Yi, Governor of Yongzhou, saw him and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of ten he was selling calendar almanacs at Zhuque Crossing when Yuan Yi, Governor of Yongzhou, saw him and was struck by the boy's unusual qualities.

sentences.zh: 顗嘗來昭所，昭讀書自若，神色不改。

translations.literal: Yi once came to Zhao's place; Zhao read as before, his expression unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi once visited Zhao's home, the boy continued reading as if nothing had happened, his composure unaltered.

sentences.zh: 顗歎曰：「此兒神情不凡，必成佳器。」

translations.literal: Yi sighed and said: "This child's spirit and expression are extraordinary; he will surely become a fine vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Yi sighed and said, "This boy's spirit and bearing are extraordinary. He is sure to become a man of great promise."

sentences.zh: 司徒建安王休仁聞而悅之，固欲致昭。

translations.literal: When Prince Jian'an Xiu Ren, Minister of Works, heard of this he was pleased and firmly wished to bring Zhao to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jian'an Xiu Ren, Minister of Works, heard of the boy, he was delighted and was determined to bring Zhao into his service.

sentences.zh: 昭以宋氏多故，遂不往。

translations.literal: Zhao, because the Song house had many troubles, then did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao declined to go, citing the many troubles afflicting the Song court.

sentences.zh: 或有稱昭于廷尉虞願，乃遣車迎昭。

translations.literal: Someone praised Zhao to Yu Yuan, Minister of Justice, who then sent a carriage to welcome Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When someone recommended Zhao to Yu Yuan, Minister of Justice, Yu sent a carriage to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 時願宗人通之在坐，並當時名流。

translations.literal: At the time Yu's clansman Tongzhi was seated there, together with other celebrated figures of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan's clansman Tongzhi was present, along with other leading figures of the day.

sentences.zh: 通之貽昭詩曰：「英妙擅山東，才子傾洛陽，清塵誰能嗣，及爾遘遺芳。」

translations.literal: Tongzhi presented Zhao with a poem saying: "Outstanding brilliance excels in Shandong; talented men fill Luoyang. Who can inherit the pure dust? I meet you and encounter lingering fragrance."
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi presented Zhao with a poem: "Outstanding talent shines in Shandong; gifted men fill Luoyang. Who can follow in the footsteps of the great? In you I find their lingering fragrance."

sentences.zh: 太原王延秀薦昭于丹陽尹袁粲，深見禮，辟為郡主簿，使諸子從昭受學。

translations.literal: Wang Yanxiu of Taiyuan recommended Zhao to Yuan Can, Prefect of Danyang, who deeply honored him, recruited him as chief clerk of the commandery, and had his sons study under Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanxiu of Taiyuan recommended Zhao to Yuan Can, Prefect of Danyang. Yuan treated him with great respect, appointed him chief clerk of the commandery, and had his sons study under Zhao.

sentences.zh: 會明帝崩，粲造哀策文，乃引昭定其所制，昭有其半焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Can composed a mourning proclamation; he then brought in Zhao to fix what he had written, and half of it was Zhao's.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Yuan Can drafted the mourning proclamation and brought Zhao in to revise it. Half of the final text was Zhao's work.

sentences.zh: 粲每經昭戶，輒歎曰：「經其戶寂若無人，披其帷其人斯在，豈非名賢。」

translations.literal: Each time Can passed Zhao's door he would sigh and say: "Passing his door it is silent as if no one were there; drawing aside the curtain, the man is there—surely a celebrated worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yuan Can passed Zhao's door he would sigh and say, "Pass his threshold and all is silent, as though no one were home; draw aside the curtain and there he sits—surely this is a man of true distinction."

sentences.zh: 尋為總明學士、奉朝請。

translations.literal: Soon he became a scholar of Zongming and Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed a scholar of Zongming and Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，累遷尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era of Qi, he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Ceremonial Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era of Qi, he rose through successive promotions to Director of the Ceremonial Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是御史中丞劉休薦昭于齊武帝，永明初，以昭為南郡王侍讀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiu had recommended Zhao to Emperor Wu of Qi; at the beginning of Yongming, Zhao was made Reader-in-Attendance to the Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiu had recommended Zhao to Emperor Wu of Qi. At the beginning of the Yongming era, Zhao was appointed Reader-in-Attendance to the Prince of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 王嗣帝位，故時臣隸爭求權寵，唯昭及南陽宗夬保身而已，守正無所參入，竟不罹禍。

translations.literal: When the prince succeeded to the throne, former retainers all strove for power and favor; only Zhao and Zong Gai of Nanyang preserved themselves, holding to rectitude and not meddling, and in the end did not suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince ascended the throne, former retainers scrambled for power and favor. Only Zhao and Zong Gai of Nanyang kept themselves safe by holding to rectitude and staying out of court intrigues, and in the end they escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 明帝踐阼，引昭為中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he brought in Zhao as General Affairs Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he appointed Zhao General Affairs Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時居此職者，皆權傾天下，昭獨廉靜無所幹豫，器服率陋，身安粗糲。

translations.literal: At that time those who held this post all wielded power that tilted the world; Zhao alone was pure and quiet, meddling in nothing, his utensils and clothing generally plain, content with coarse fare.
translations.idiomatic: At that time those who held this post wielded enormous power, but Zhao alone remained incorruptible and aloof from intrigue. His furnishings and clothing were plain, and he was content with simple food.

sentences.zh: 常插燭板床，明帝聞之，賜漆合燭盤，敕曰：「卿有古人之風，故賜卿古人之物。」

translations.literal: He often stuck candles into a plain board bed. When Emperor Ming heard of this, he granted him a lacquered candle holder and tray, instructing: "You have the air of the ancients; therefore I grant you the things of the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: He often stuck candles into a plain wooden bed. When Emperor Ming heard of this, he sent him a lacquered candle holder and tray with the message, "You have the spirit of the ancients, so I give you the furnishings of the ancients."

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝素重昭，梁台建，以為給事黃門侍郎，領著作，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang had long esteemed Zhao. When the Liang administration was established, he was made Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently overseeing the Bureau of Compilation and serving as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang had long held Zhao in high regard. When the Liang administration was established, he appointed him Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently overseeing the Bureau of Compilation and serving as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，兼五兵尚書，參選事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian, he concurrently served as Minister of War and took part in selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianjian, he was additionally appointed Minister of War and participated in the selection of officials.

sentences.zh: 四年即真。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 歷位左戶尚書，安成內史。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister of the Left Household and Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Minister of the Left Household and Administrator of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 郡自宋來，兵亂相接，府舍稱凶。

translations.literal: Since the Song, the commandery had suffered continuous military turmoil, and the official residence was said to be inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Song dynasty the commandery had been ravaged by continuous warfare, and the official residence was considered haunted.

sentences.zh: 每昏旦間，人鬼相觸，在任者鮮以吉終。

translations.literal: Every dusk and dawn, the living and ghosts encountered one another; those who held office rarely ended well.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk and dawn the living and the dead were said to mingle there, and few who held the post met a peaceful end.

sentences.zh: 及昭至，有人夜見甲兵出，曰：「傅公善人，不可侵犯。」

translations.literal: When Zhao arrived, someone at night saw armored soldiers emerge and say: "Master Fu is a good man; he must not be violated."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao arrived, someone saw armored soldiers emerge at night, saying, "Master Fu is a good man and must not be harmed."

sentences.zh: 乃騰虛而去。

translations.literal: They then soared into the void and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They then vanished into the air and departed.

sentences.zh: 有頃風雨總至，飄郡聽事入隍中，自是郡遂無患，咸以昭貞正所致。

translations.literal: Before long wind and rain came together and blew the commandery hall into the moat; from then on the commandery had no further trouble, and all attributed it to Zhao's integrity and rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a storm arose and blew the commandery hall into the moat. From that time the commandery was free of trouble, and all attributed this to Zhao's upright character.

sentences.zh: 郡溪無魚，或有暑月薦昭魚者，昭既不納，又不欲拒，遂餧於門側。

translations.literal: The streams of the commandery had no fish; sometimes in summer months someone would present fish to Zhao. Zhao neither accepted them nor wished to refuse outright, so he fed them beside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The streams of the commandery had no fish, yet in summer someone once presented fish to Zhao. Unwilling either to accept the gift or to reject the giver outright, he fed the fish beside his gate.

sentences.zh: 郡多猛獸為害，常設檻阱，昭曰：「人不害猛獸，猛獸亦不害人。」

translations.literal: The commandery had many fierce beasts that caused harm; traps were constantly set. Zhao said: "If men do not harm fierce beasts, fierce beasts also will not harm men."
translations.idiomatic: Fierce beasts often ravaged the commandery, and traps were constantly set for them. Zhao said, "If men do not harm fierce beasts, the beasts will not harm men either."

sentences.zh: 乃命去檻阱，猛獸竟不為害。

translations.literal: He then ordered the traps removed, and the fierce beasts in the end did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the traps removed, and the fierce beasts ceased to cause harm.

sentences.zh: 曆秘書監，太常卿，遷臨海太守。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director of the Palace Library and Minister of Ceremonies, then was transferred to Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Director of the Palace Library and Minister of Ceremonies, then was transferred to Administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 郡有蜜岩，前後太守皆自封固，專收其利。

translations.literal: The commandery had a Honey Cliff; successive administrators all sealed and enclosed it, monopolizing its profits.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had a Honey Cliff that successive administrators had sealed off for their private profit.

sentences.zh: 昭以周文之囿，與百姓共之，大可喻小，乃教勿封。

translations.literal: Zhao, citing King Wen's park shared with the common people—the large can illustrate the small—instructed that it not be sealed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cited the example of King Wen's park, shared with the people, arguing that what holds for the great applies to the small, and ordered that the cliff not be sealed.

sentences.zh: 縣令嘗餉栗，置絹于薄下，昭笑而還之。

translations.literal: A magistrate once presented chestnuts with silk placed beneath the record book; Zhao smiled and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: A magistrate once presented chestnuts with silk hidden beneath the record book. Zhao smiled and returned the gift.

sentences.zh: 普通五年，為散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Putong, he was Regular Attendant and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Putong he was appointed Regular Attendant and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 昭所蒞官，常以清靜為政，不尚嚴肅。

translations.literal: In every office Zhao attended, he always governed with clarity and quiet, not prizing severity.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held, Zhao governed with calm restraint rather than harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 居朝廷，無所請謁，不畜私門生，不交私利。

translations.literal: In the court he made no requests or visits, kept no private disciples, and had no dealings for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: At court he made no solicitations, kept no private disciples, and engaged in no dealings for personal profit.

sentences.zh: 終日端居，以書記為樂，雖老不衰。

translations.literal: All day he sat upright, taking books and writing as his pleasure; even in old age he did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days in quiet study, finding his pleasure in books and writing, and never lost this enthusiasm even in old age.

sentences.zh: 博極古今，尤善人物，魏、晉以來，官宦簿閥，姻通內外，舉而論之，無所遺失，世稱為學府。

translations.literal: Broadly reaching to the limits of ancient and modern, he was especially skilled in persons: from Wei and Jin onward, official registers and clan pedigrees, marriage ties within and without—raising and discussing them, nothing was omitted; the age called him a storehouse of learning.
translations.idiomatic: His learning spanned all ages, and he was especially expert on people. From the Wei and Jin dynasties onward, he could discuss official genealogies, clan pedigrees, and marriage alliances without omitting a detail. The age called him a living library.

sentences.zh: 性尤篤慎，子婦嘗得家餉牛肉以進昭，昭召其子曰：「食之則犯法，告之則不可。

translations.literal: His nature was especially sincere and cautious. His daughter-in-law once received beef from her family as a gift and presented it to Zhao. Zhao summoned his son and said: "To eat it would violate the law; to report it would not do.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially conscientious and cautious. When his daughter-in-law once received beef from her family and presented it to him, Zhao summoned his son and said, "To eat it would violate the law, yet to report the gift would be unthinkable.

sentences.zh: 取而埋之。」

translations.literal: Take it and bury it."
translations.idiomatic: Take it and bury it."

sentences.zh: 其居身行己，不負闇室，類皆如此。

translations.literal: In his personal conduct he did not betray even a dark room; most things were like this.
translations.idiomatic: In his personal conduct he was upright even when no one was watching; most of his actions were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 後進宗其學，重其道，人人自以為不逮。

translations.literal: Later generations honored his learning and esteemed his way; each person felt himself unable to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Younger scholars revered his learning and honored his character; each felt himself unable to measure up.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was given the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 長子諝，位尚書郎，湘東王外兵參軍。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xu held the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Military Affairs Aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xu served as Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Military Affairs Aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 諝子准有文才，梁宣帝時，位度支尚書。

translations.literal: Xu's son Zhun had literary talent; in the time of Emperor Xuan of Liang he held the post of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Zhun was a man of literary talent who, under Emperor Xuan of Liang, served as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 昭弟映字徽遠，三歲而孤。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Ying, styled Huiyuan, was orphaned at three.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Ying, styled Huiyuan, was orphaned at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 兄弟友睦，修身勵行，非禮不動。

translations.literal: The brothers were friendly and harmonious, cultivating themselves and encouraging conduct; they would not act against ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were devoted to one another, cultivating themselves in conduct and moving only according to proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 始昭之守臨海，陸倕餞之，賓主俱歡，日暮不反。

translations.literal: When Zhao first went to serve as Administrator of Linhai, Lu Chui saw him off; host and guest were both joyful and did not return until dusk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao first departed to serve as Administrator of Linhai, Lu Chui gave him a farewell banquet. Host and guest were so merry that evening fell before Zhao returned home.

sentences.zh: 映以昭年高，不可連夜極樂，乃自往候接，同乘而歸。

translations.literal: Ying, because Zhao was advanced in years and should not revel through the night, went himself to meet him, and they returned together in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, thinking that Zhao was too old to stay out reveling all night, went himself to fetch his brother, and they rode home together.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並已斑白，時人美而服焉。

translations.literal: Both brothers' hair was already streaked with white; people of the time admired and submitted to this.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers' hair was already white. People of the time admired their devotion.

sentences.zh: 及昭卒，映喪之如父，年踰七十，哀戚過禮，服制雖除，每言輒慟。

translations.literal: When Zhao died, Ying mourned him as for a father. Though over seventy, his grief exceeded the rites; though the mourning garments were removed, whenever he spoke he would sob.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao died, Ying mourned him as he would a father. Though over seventy, his grief exceeded what the rites required. Even after the mourning period ended, he wept whenever he spoke of his brother.

sentences.zh: 天監中，位烏程令，卒于太中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era he held the post of magistrate of Wucheng and died as Grand Master for All-Purpose.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjian era he served as magistrate of Wucheng and died while holding the rank of Grand Master for All-Purpose.

sentences.zh: 子弘。

translations.literal: His son was Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hong.

sentences.zh: 孔休源字慶緒，會稽山陰人，晉尚書沖之八世孫，沖即開府儀同三司愉之世父也。

translations.literal: Kong Xiuyuan, styled Qingxu, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji, eighth-generation descendant of Chongzhi, Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Jin; Chong was the paternal uncle by generation of Yu, Grand Minister with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xiuyuan, styled Qingxu, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji and an eighth-generation descendant of Chongzhi, Director of the Imperial Secretariat under the Jin dynasty. Chong was the paternal uncle of Yu, who held the rank of Grand Minister with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 曾祖遙之，宋尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Yaozhi, Director of the Water Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yaozhi served as Director of the Water Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat under the Song dynasty.

sentences.zh: 父佩，齊通直郎。

translations.literal: His father Pei was Attendant for Direct Communication under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pei served as Attendant for Direct Communication under the Qi dynasty.

sentences.zh: 休源十一而孤，居喪盡禮，每見父手所寫書，必哀慟流涕不能自勝，見者莫不為之垂泣。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan was orphaned at eleven; he observed mourning to the full rites. Whenever he saw books written in his father's hand, he would mourn and weep beyond control; those who saw it all wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyuan was orphaned at eleven and observed the mourning rites with complete devotion. Whenever he saw books written in his father's hand, he would weep uncontrollably, and those who witnessed his grief wept with him.

sentences.zh: 後就吳興沈麟士受經，略通大義。

translations.literal: Later he studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a general grasp of their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a general understanding of their essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，太尉徐孝嗣省其策，深善之，謂同坐曰：「董仲舒、華令思何以尚此，可謂後生之准的也。

translations.literal: The province recommended him as a cultivated talent. Grand Commandant Xu Xiaosi examined his examination answer and deeply approved it, saying to those seated with him: "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He may be called the target for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The province recommended him as a cultivated talent. Grand Commandant Xu Xiaosi examined his examination answer and was deeply impressed, saying to those present, "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He is a standard by which later generations may be measured.

sentences.zh: 觀此足稱王佐之才。」

translations.literal: Judging from this, he fully deserves to be called talent for assisting a king."
translations.idiomatic: From this one can see that he truly possesses the talent of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 琅邪王融雅相友善，乃薦之于司徒竟陵王，為西邸學士。

translations.literal: Wang Rong of Langya was elegantly friendly with him and recommended him to Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, as a scholar of the Western Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong of Langya became his close friend and recommended him to Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, who appointed him a scholar of the Western Lodge.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，與南陽劉之遴同為太學博士，當時以為美選。

translations.literal: When the Liang administration was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang both served as erudites of the Imperial University; at the time this was considered a fine selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang administration was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang were both appointed erudites of the Imperial University, a pairing widely regarded as an excellent choice.

sentences.zh: 休源初到都，寓於宗人少府孔登。

translations.literal: When Xiuyuan first arrived in the capital, he lodged with his clansman Kong Deng, Director of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuyuan first arrived in the capital, he stayed with his clansman Kong Deng, Director of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 曾以祠事入廟，侍中範雲一與相遇，深加褒賞，曰：「不期忽覯清顏，頓祛鄙吝，觀天披霧，驗之今日。」

translations.literal: Once, on temple business he entered the shrine and chanced to meet Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, who deeply praised him, saying: "Unexpectedly I suddenly behold your clear countenance; at once my vulgar parsimony is dispelled. To view heaven through parting clouds—today I verify it."
translations.idiomatic: Once, while entering a shrine on temple business, he chanced to meet Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, who praised him warmly, saying, "I never expected to meet you here. Your presence dispels my petty narrowness at once. It is like seeing the sky through parting clouds—and today I have proved it."

sentences.zh: 後雲命駕到少府，登便拂筵整帶，謂當詣己，備水陸之品。

translations.literal: Later Yun ordered his carriage to the Palace Treasury. Deng at once brushed the mat and straightened his belt, thinking Yun was coming to him, and prepared delicacies of land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fan Yun ordered his carriage to the Palace Treasury. Kong Deng immediately brushed the mat and straightened his belt, assuming the visit was for him, and prepared an elaborate feast of land and sea delicacies.

sentences.zh: 雲駐箸命休源，及至，命取其常膳，止有赤倉米飯，蒸鮑魚。

translations.literal: Yun stopped his chopsticks and summoned Xiuyuan. When he arrived, Yun ordered his usual meal brought—only red-grain rice and steamed abalone.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun put down his chopsticks and summoned Xiuyuan instead. When Xiuyuan arrived, Yun asked for his usual meal—nothing but plain red-grain rice and steamed abalone.

sentences.zh: 雲食休源食，不舉主人之饌。

translations.literal: Yun ate Xiuyuan's food and did not touch the host's fare.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun ate Xiuyuan's simple meal and did not touch the feast Kong Deng had prepared.

sentences.zh: 高談盡日，同載還家。

translations.literal: They talked loftily all day and returned home in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: They talked at length all day and rode home together in the same carriage.

sentences.zh: 登深以為愧。

translations.literal: Deng was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Deng was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 尚書令沈約當朝貴顯，軒蓋盈門，休源或時後來，必虛襟引接，處之坐右，商略文義。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue was eminent and honored in the court; carriages filled his gate. When Xiuyuan sometimes came later, Yue always received him with open heart, seated him at his right, and discussed literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue was one of the most eminent men at court, and carriages filled his gate. Whenever Xiuyuan arrived late, Yue received him with open warmth, seated him at his right hand, and discussed literature with him.

sentences.zh: 其為通人所推如此。

translations.literal: This was how he was esteemed by men of understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which men of discernment held him.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗問吏部尚書徐勉求一有學藝解朝儀者，為尚書儀曹郎，勉曰：「孔休源識見清通，詳練故事，自晉、宋起居注，誦略上口。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Minister of the Personnel Bureau Xu Mian to find someone learned in arts who understood court ritual to serve as Director of the Ceremonial Bureau. Mian said: "Kong Xiuyuan's knowledge and insight are clear and penetrating; he is thoroughly versed in precedents. From the Jin and Song daily records onward, he can recite them from memory."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked Minister of the Personnel Bureau Xu Mian to find a learned man who understood court ritual for the post of Director of the Ceremonial Bureau. Mian replied, "Kong Xiuyuan has clear and penetrating insight and is thoroughly versed in precedent. From the Jin and Song daily records onward, he can recite them from memory."

sentences.zh: 武帝亦素聞之，即日除兼尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had also long heard of him and that same day appointed him concurrently Director of the Ceremonial Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had also long heard of him and appointed him that same day as concurrent Director of the Ceremonial Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時多所改作，每逮訪前事，休源即以所誦記隨機斷決，曾無疑滯。

translations.literal: At the time many reforms were made; whenever earlier matters were consulted, Xiuyuan would decide on the spot from what he had memorized, never hesitating.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many reforms were underway. Whenever earlier precedents were consulted, Xiuyuan decided on the spot from memory, never hesitating.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎任昉常謂之為「孔獨誦」。

translations.literal: Director of the Personnel Bureau Ren Fang often called him "Kong the Sole Reciter."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Personnel Bureau Ren Fang often called him "Kong the Sole Reciter."

sentences.zh: 遷建康獄正，平反辯析，時罕冤人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Warden of Jiankang Prison, overturning wrongful verdicts and analyzing cases; at the time few innocent people suffered injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Warden of Jiankang Prison, where he overturned wrongful verdicts and analyzed cases with such care that few innocent people were wronged.

sentences.zh: 後有選人為獄司者，帝常引休源以勵之。

translations.literal: Later, when someone was selected for prison administration, the emperor often cited Xiuyuan to encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, whenever someone was appointed to prison administration, the emperor would cite Xiuyuan as an example to encourage him.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左丞，彈肅禮闈，雅允朝望。

translations.literal: Later he became Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enforcing discipline in the examination halls and fully meeting the court's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enforcing discipline in the examination halls and fully meeting the court's expectations.

sentences.zh: 時周舍撰禮疑義，自漢、魏至於齊、梁，並皆搜采，休源所有奏議，咸預編錄。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou She compiled doubtful points in ritual, searching from Han and Wei through Qi and Liang; all of Xiuyuan's memorials and proposals were included in the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhou She was compiling doubtful points in ritual, gathering material from Han and Wei through Qi and Liang. All of Xiuyuan's memorials and proposals were included in the work.

sentences.zh: 再遷長兼御史中丞，正色直繩，無所回避，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to serve concurrently as Censor-in-Chief; with stern countenance he upheld the law straight, shrinking from nothing, and the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to serve concurrently as Censor-in-Chief. With stern countenance he upheld the law without flinching, and the officials feared him.

sentences.zh: 後為晉安王長史、南郡太守，行荊州府州事。

translations.literal: Later he served as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an and Administrator of Nanjun, administering the affairs of the Jingzhou prefecture and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an and Administrator of Nanjun, administering the affairs of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「荊州總上流沖要，義高分陝，今以十歲兒委卿，善匡翼之，勿憚周昌之舉也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "Jingzhou commands the upper reaches and is strategically vital; its importance equals the partition at Shan. Now I entrust a ten-year-old boy to you. Guide and support him well, and do not shrink from acting like Zhou Chang."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "Jingzhou commands the upper Yangzi and is strategically vital; its importance equals the partition at Shan. I now entrust a ten-year-old boy to you. Guide and support him well, and do not shrink from acting like Zhou Chang."

sentences.zh: 乃敕晉安王曰：「孔休源人倫儀錶，汝年尚幼，當每事師之。」

translations.literal: He then instructed Prince Jin'an: "Kong Xiuyuan is a model of human conduct. You are still young; in every matter you should take him as your teacher."
translations.idiomatic: He then instructed Prince Jin'an, "Kong Xiuyuan is a model of human conduct. You are still young; in every matter you should take him as your teacher."

sentences.zh: 尋始興王憺代鎮荊州，復為憺府長史，太守、行府事如故。

translations.literal: Soon Prince Shixing Dan replaced him as commander of Jingzhou; Xiuyuan again served as chief clerk to Dan's administration, with his posts as Administrator and acting prefectural affairs unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince Shixing Dan replaced him as commander of Jingzhou. Xiuyuan again served as chief clerk to Dan's administration, retaining his posts as Administrator and acting prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 在州累政，甚有政績，平心決斷，請托弗行。

translations.literal: Through successive terms in the province he achieved notable administrative results, deciding cases with impartial heart and refusing to grant requests through connections.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive terms in the province he achieved notable results, deciding cases impartially and refusing to grant requests through connections.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 曆秘書監，復為晉安王府長史、南蘭陵太守，別敕專行南徐州事。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director of the Palace Library, then again as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an's household and Administrator of Nanlanling, with a separate edict appointing him solely to administer South Xuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Director of the Palace Library, then again as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an's household and Administrator of Nanlanling, with a separate edict appointing him solely to administer South Xuzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 休源累佐名蕃，甚得人譽，王深相倚仗，常於中齋別施一榻，云：「此是孔長史坐」，人莫得預焉，其見敬如此。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan repeatedly assisted famous princely domains and won great public esteem. The prince deeply relied on him and always placed a separate couch in the inner study, saying: "This is Chief Clerk Kong's seat." No one else was permitted there; such was the respect shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyuan repeatedly assisted distinguished princely domains and won great public esteem. The prince relied on him deeply and always placed a separate couch in the inner study, saying, "This is Chief Clerk Kong's seat." No one else was permitted to use it; such was the respect shown him.

sentences.zh: 曆都官尚書。

translations.literal: He successively served as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 普通七年，揚州刺史臨川王宏薨，武帝與群臣議代居州任者，時貴戚王公咸望遷授。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, Prince Linchuan Hong, Governor of Yangzhou, died. Emperor Wu discussed with his ministers who should replace him in the provincial post; at the time noble princes and royal kin all hoped for transfer and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Putong, Prince Linchuan Hong, Governor of Yangzhou, died. Emperor Wu discussed with his ministers who should replace him; at the time noble princes and royal kin all hoped for the appointment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕已得人，孔休源才識通敏，實應此選。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I already have my man. Kong Xiuyuan's talent and insight are penetrating and keen; he truly fits this selection."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I already have my man. Kong Xiuyuan's talent and insight are penetrating and keen; he truly fits this appointment."

sentences.zh: 乃授宣惠將軍、監揚州事。

translations.literal: He then granted him the title General Who Proclaims Grace and Supervisor of Yangzhou Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed him General Who Proclaims Grace and Supervisor of Yangzhou Affairs.

sentences.zh: 休源初為臨川王行佐，及王薨而管州任，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan had first served as Prince Linchuan's administrative aide; when the prince died he took charge of the provincial post, and public opinion honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyuan had first served as Prince Linchuan's administrative aide; when the prince died he took charge of the province, and public opinion regarded this as an honor.

sentences.zh: 神州都會，簿領殷繁，休源剖斷如流，傍無私謁。

translations.literal: The imperial region's great metropolis had abundant records and documents; Xiuyuan cut through them like flowing water, with no private solicitations at his side.
translations.idiomatic: In the imperial region's great metropolis, with its abundant records and documents, Xiuyuan cut through cases like flowing water and accepted no private solicitations.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong, Xiuyuan was additionally appointed Grandee of Golden Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongdatong, Xiuyuan was additionally appointed Grandee of Golden Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 在州晝決辭訟，夜覽墳籍。

translations.literal: While in the province, by day he decided pleadings and lawsuits, and by night he read ancient texts.
translations.idiomatic: While in the province, by day he decided pleadings and lawsuits, and by night he read ancient texts.

sentences.zh: 每車駕巡幸，常以軍國事委之。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went on inspection tours, the emperor always entrusted military and state affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on inspection tours, he always entrusted military and state affairs to Xiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子薨，有敕夜召休源入宴居殿與群公參定謀議，立晉安王綱為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, there was an edict summoning Xiuyuan by night into the Yanju Hall to participate with the assembled dukes in settling the deliberations, and Prince Gang of Jinan was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, an edict summoned Xiuyuan by night into the Yanju Hall to join the assembled dukes in settling policy, and Prince Gang of Jinan was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 自公卿珥貂插筆奏決於休源前，休源怡然無愧，時人名為兼天子。

translations.literal: From dukes and ministers with marten-tail ornaments and inserted writing brushes, all submitted decisions before Xiuyuan; Xiuyuan was calm and without shame, and people of the time called him the concurrent Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and ministers, with marten-tail ornaments and writing brushes tucked in their caps, submitted decisions before Xiuyuan. Xiuyuan remained calm and unembarrassed, and people of the time called him the concurrent Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，遺令薄葬，節朔薦蔬菲而已。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he died; his final instructions ordered a simple burial and only offerings of vegetables and humble fare at seasonal and new-moon rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he died. His final instructions ordered a simple burial and only offerings of vegetables and humble fare at seasonal and new-moon rites.

sentences.zh: 帝為之流涕，顧謝舉曰：「孔休源居職清忠，方欲共康政道，奄至隕沒，朕甚痛之。」

translations.literal: The emperor shed tears for him, turned to Xie Ju, and said, "Kong Xiuyuan held office with purity and loyalty; I was just about to join him in bringing health to the Way of government, when suddenly he fell and died. We are deeply pained by it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shed tears for him, turned to Xie Ju, and said, "Kong Xiuyuan held office with purity and loyalty; I was just about to work with him to bring health to government, when suddenly he fell and died. We are deeply pained by it."

sentences.zh: 舉曰：「此人清介強直，臣竊為陛下惜之。」

translations.literal: Ju said, "This man was pure, principled, forceful, and upright; your subject privately grieves over him for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "This man was pure, principled, forceful, and upright; your subject privately grieves over him for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Viscount Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Viscount Zhen.

sentences.zh: 休源風範強正，明練政體，常以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan's bearing was forceful and upright; he was clear and practiced in the substance of government, and always took the empire as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyuan's bearing was forceful and upright. Clear and practiced in the substance of government, he always took the welfare of the empire as his personal responsibility.

sentences.zh: 武帝深委仗之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu deeply entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 累居顯職，性縝密，未嘗言禁中事。

translations.literal: Through successive eminent posts, his nature was meticulous; he never spoke of affairs within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive eminent posts, he remained meticulous by nature and never spoke of affairs within the palace.

sentences.zh: 聚書盈七千卷，手自校練。

translations.literal: He collected more than seven thousand scrolls of books and personally collated and corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: He collected more than seven thousand scrolls of books and personally collated and corrected them.

sentences.zh: 凡奏議彈文勒成十五卷。

translations.literal: In all, his memorials, proposals, and impeachments were compiled into fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials, proposals, and impeachments were compiled into fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 長子雲章頗有父風，位東揚州別駕。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yunzhang largely had his father's character and held the post of Vice Administrator of East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yunzhang largely inherited his father's character and served as Vice Administrator of East Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少子宗范聰敏有識度，位中書郎。

translations.literal: His younger son Zongfan was intelligent and perceptive and held the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Zongfan was intelligent and perceptive and served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江革字休映，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖齊之，宋都水使者，尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Qizhi, Commissioner of Waterways under Song and Director of the Gold Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qizhi served as Commissioner of Waterways under the Song dynasty and as Director of the Gold Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父柔之，齊尚書倉部郎，有孝行，以母憂毀卒。

translations.literal: His father Rouzhi was Director of the Granary Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat under Qi, a man of filial conduct who died from grief during his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rouzhi served as Director of the Granary Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat under the Qi dynasty. A man of filial devotion, he died from grief during his mother's mourning period.

sentences.zh: 革幼而聰敏，早有才思，六歲便解屬文。

translations.literal: Ge from youth was intelligent and keen; early he had literary talent, and at six he could already compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was intelligent from childhood and showed early literary talent; at the age of six he could already compose prose.

sentences.zh: 柔之深加賞器，曰：「此兒必興吾門。」

translations.literal: Rouzhi deeply admired him, saying: "This child will surely raise up our house."
translations.idiomatic: Rouzhi admired him deeply, saying, "This boy will surely bring honor to our house."

sentences.zh: 九歲丁父艱，與第四弟觀同生，少孤貧，傍無師友，兄弟自相訓勖，讀書精力不倦。

translations.literal: At nine he entered mourning for his father. He and his fourth younger brother Guan were born of the same mother; orphaned young and poor, with no teachers or friends nearby, the brothers encouraged each other in study, reading with tireless energy.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he entered mourning for his father. He and his fourth younger brother Guan, born of the same mother, were orphaned young and poor, with no teachers or friends nearby. The brothers encouraged each other in study and read with tireless energy.

sentences.zh: 十六喪母，以孝聞。

translations.literal: At sixteen his mother died; he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died at sixteen, he became renowned for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 服闋，與觀俱詣太學，補國子生，舉高第。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he and Guan both went to the Imperial University, were enrolled as students of the National University, and were recommended with highest marks.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he and Guan both entered the Imperial University as students of the National University and were recommended with the highest marks.

sentences.zh: 齊中書郎王融、吏部郎謝朓雅相欽重。

translations.literal: Wang Rong, Director of the Secretariat under Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Personnel Bureau, both deeply admired and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, Director of the Secretariat under Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Personnel Bureau, both deeply admired and esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 朓嘗行還過候革，時大寒雪，見革弊絮單席，而耽學不倦，嗟歎久之，乃脫其所著襦，並手割半氈與革充臥具而去。

translations.literal: Tiao once returned from a journey and stopped to visit Ge. It was bitterly cold with snow; he saw Ge in worn cotton and on a single mat, yet devoted to study without weariness. Tiao sighed long, then took off his own padded jacket and with his own hands cut half a felt rug to serve as Ge's bedding before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao once returned from a journey and stopped to visit Ge. It was bitterly cold and snowing; he found Ge in worn cotton clothing on a single mat, yet still devoted to study without rest. Tiao sighed at length, then took off his own padded jacket and cut half a felt rug by hand to serve as Ge's bedding before departing.

sentences.zh: 司徒竟陵王聞其名，引為西邸學士。

translations.literal: Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, heard his name and recruited him as a scholar of the Western Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, heard of him and recruited him as a scholar of the Western Lodge.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉南徐州秀才。

translations.literal: At his capping he was recommended as a cultivated talent of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he was recommended as a cultivated talent of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時豫章胡諧之行州事，王融與諧之書令薦革。

translations.literal: At the time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting in provincial affairs; Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting in provincial affairs. Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.

sentences.zh: 諧之方貢琅邪王泛，便以革代之。

translations.literal: Xiezhi had just presented Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and therefore replaced him with Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi had just presented Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and therefore substituted Ge in his place.

sentences.zh: 僕射江祏深相引接，祏為太子詹事，啟革為丞。

translations.literal: Vice Director Jiang Si deeply received and welcomed him. When Si became Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, he recommended Ge as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Jiang Si received him warmly. When Si became Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, he recommended Ge as assistant.

sentences.zh: 祏時權傾朝右，以革才堪經國，令參掌機務，詔誥文檄皆委以具。

translations.literal: At the time Si's power tilted the right side of the court; considering Ge's talent fit for governing the state, he had him take part in managing secret affairs. Edicts, proclamations, and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Si wielded enormous power at court. Considering Ge's talent fit for governing the state, he had him take part in managing secret affairs. Edicts, proclamations, and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.

sentences.zh: 革防杜形跡，外人不知。

translations.literal: Ge guarded against revealing traces; outsiders did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Ge kept his involvement concealed, and outsiders knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 祏誅，賓客皆罹其罪，革獨以智免。

translations.literal: When Si was executed, his retainers all suffered for the crime; Ge alone escaped through wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: When Si was executed, his retainers all suffered for the crime, but Ge alone escaped through his shrewdness.

sentences.zh: 除尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，梁武帝入石頭，時吳興太守袁昂據郡拒義不從，革制書與昂，于坐立成，辭義典雅，帝深賞歎之，令與徐勉同掌書記。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing, Emperor Wu of Liang entered Shitou. At the time Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery and refused to follow the righteous cause. Ge drafted a letter to Ang, completing it while seated; its language and meaning were elegant and classical. The emperor deeply admired it and ordered him to manage records together with Xu Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing, Emperor Wu of Liang entered Shitou. At the time Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery and refused to submit. Ge drafted a letter to Ang, completing it while seated; its language and meaning were elegant and classical. The emperor admired it deeply and ordered him to manage records together with Xu Mian.

sentences.zh: 建安王為雍州刺史，表求管記，以革為征北記室參軍，帶中廬令。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an became Governor of Yongzhou and memorialized requesting a records officer; Ge was made Military Affairs Secretary to the Campaign North and concurrently Director of the Central Stable.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an became Governor of Yongzhou and memorialized requesting a records officer. Ge was appointed Military Affairs Secretary to the Campaign North and concurrently Director of the Central Stable.

sentences.zh: 與弟觀少長共居，不忍離別，苦求同行。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Guan had lived together from youth to adulthood and could not bear to part; he earnestly begged to travel together.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Guan had lived together from youth and could not bear to part; he earnestly begged to travel together.

sentences.zh: 以觀為征北行參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: Guan was made Acting Military Affairs Aide to the Campaign North and concurrently records officer.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was appointed Acting Military Affairs Aide to the Campaign North and concurrently records officer.

sentences.zh: 時吳興沈約、樂安任昉與革書云：「比聞雍府妙選英才，文房之職，總卿昆季，可謂馭二龍於長途，騁騏驥於千里。」

translations.literal: At the time Shen Yue of Wuxing and Ren Fang of Le'an wrote to Ge: "We have lately heard that the Yongzhou administration finely selects outstanding talent. The literary posts are entrusted to you and your brother—one may say driving two dragons on a long road, letting thoroughbreds run a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shen Yue of Wuxing and Ren Fang of Le'an wrote to Ge, "We have lately heard that the Yongzhou administration has finely selected outstanding talent. The literary posts are entrusted to you and your brother—like driving two dragons on a long road, or letting thoroughbreds run a thousand li."

sentences.zh: 途次江夏，觀卒。

translations.literal: On the way, passing Jiangxia, Guan died.
translations.idiomatic: On the way, passing Jiangxia, Guan died.

sentences.zh: 革在雍州，為府王所禮，款若布衣。

translations.literal: Ge was in Yongzhou, treated with courtesy by the prince of the domain, intimate as a common cloth-clad man.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzhou, Ge was treated with courtesy by the prince of the domain, who received him with the warmth due an old friend.

sentences.zh: 後為建康正，頻遷秣陵、建康令，為政明肅，豪強憚之。

translations.literal: Later he was Warden of Jiankang, then repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Moling and Jiankang; his governance was clear and stern, and the powerful feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Warden of Jiankang, then was repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Moling and Jiankang. His governance was clear and stern, and the powerful feared him.

sentences.zh: 曆中書舍人，尚書左丞，晉安王長史、尋陽太守，行江州府事。

translations.literal: He successively served as Attendant of the Secretariat, Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, chief clerk to Prince Jin'an, Administrator of Xunyang, and administered the affairs of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Attendant of the Secretariat, Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, chief clerk to Prince Jin'an, Administrator of Xunyang, and administrator of Jiangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 徙廬陵王長史，太守、行事如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Luling; his posts as Administrator and acting affairs remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Luling, retaining his posts as Administrator and acting affairs.

sentences.zh: 以清嚴為屬城所憚。

translations.literal: For his clarity and severity he was feared by the subordinate commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His clarity and severity were feared throughout the subordinate commanderies.

sentences.zh: 時少王行事，多傾意于簽帥，革以正直自居，不與典簽趙道智坐。

translations.literal: At the time the young prince in acting affairs often favored the chief clerk; Ge held himself upright and would not sit with Chief Clerk Zhao Daozhi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the young prince in acting affairs often favored the chief clerk. Ge held himself upright and would not sit with Chief Clerk Zhao Daozhi.

sentences.zh: 道智因還都啟事，面陳革墮事好酒，以琅邪王曇聰代為行事。

translations.literal: Daozhi therefore returned to the capital to report, stating face to face that Ge neglected affairs and loved wine, and had Prince Tancong of Langya replace him in acting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhi therefore returned to the capital to report, stating face to face that Ge neglected affairs and loved wine, and had Prince Tancong of Langya replace him in acting affairs.

sentences.zh: 南州士庶為之語曰：「故人不道智，新人佞散騎，莫知度不度，新人不如故。」

translations.literal: The gentry and common people of the southern provinces made a saying: "The old man was not Daozhi; the new man is the fawning Regular Attendant. Who knows whether he measures up or not—the new man is not as good as the old."
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and common people of the southern provinces composed a saying: "The old man was not Daozhi; the new man is the fawning Regular Attendant. Who knows whether he measures up—the new man is not as good as the old."

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，彈奏豪權，一無所避。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, impeaching powerful families and yielding to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, impeaching powerful families without flinching.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮北豫章王長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Later he served as chief clerk to Prince Yuzhang of Campaign North and Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief clerk to Prince Yuzhang of Campaign North and Administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 時魏徐州刺史元法僧降附，革被敕隨府王鎮彭城。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Faseng, Governor of Xuzhou under Wei, surrendered and submitted; Ge was ordered by edict to follow the prince of the domain in garrisoning Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Faseng, Governor of Xuzhou under Wei, surrendered and submitted. Ge was ordered by edict to follow the prince of the domain in garrisoning Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 城既失守，革素不便馬，泛舟而還。

translations.literal: When the city was lost, Ge had never been comfortable on horseback and returned by boat.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Ge, who had never been comfortable on horseback, returned by boat.

sentences.zh: 途經下邳，為魏人所執。

translations.literal: Passing through Xiapi on the way, he was seized by Wei men.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Xiapi on the way, he was captured by Wei troops.

sentences.zh: 魏徐州刺史安豐王延明聞革才名，厚加接待。

translations.literal: Yanming, Prince of Anfeng and Governor of Xuzhou under Wei, heard of Ge's literary reputation and treated him with great hospitality.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming, Prince of Anfeng and Governor of Xuzhou under Wei, heard of Ge's literary reputation and treated him with great hospitality.

sentences.zh: 革稱腳疾不拜，延明將害之，見革辭色嚴正，更加敬重。

translations.literal: Ge claimed foot ailment and would not bow. Yanming was about to harm him, but seeing Ge's words and expression stern and upright, he respected him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Ge claimed a foot ailment and refused to bow. Yanming was about to harm him, but seeing Ge's stern and upright bearing, he respected him all the more.

sentences.zh: 時祖搄同被拘縶，延明使搄作欹器漏刻銘，革唾駡搄曰：「卿荷國厚恩，已無報答，乃為虜立銘，孤負朝廷。」

translations.literal: At the time Zu Chong was also detained. Yanming had Chong compose an inscription for an tilting vessel and clepsydra. Ge spat and reviled Chong, saying: "You received the state's deep grace and have no way to repay it, yet you compose an inscription for the captors—you have betrayed the court."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zu Chong was also detained. Yanming had Chong compose an inscription for a tilting vessel and clepsydra. Ge spat and reviled him, saying, "You received the state's deep grace and have no way to repay it, yet you compose an inscription for the captors—you have betrayed the court."

sentences.zh: 延明聞之，乃令革作丈八寺碑並祭彭祖文，革辭以囚執既久，無復心思。

translations.literal: When Yanming heard this, he ordered Ge to compose an inscription for the Zhangba Temple and a sacrificial text to Peng Zu. Ge declined, saying that long imprisonment had left him without further thought.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanming heard this, he ordered Ge to compose an inscription for the Zhangba Temple and a sacrificial text to Peng Zu. Ge declined, saying that long imprisonment had left him without the heart to write.

sentences.zh: 延明將加棰撲，革厲色曰：「江革行年六十，不能殺身報主，今日得死為幸，誓不為人執筆。」

translations.literal: Yanming was about to beat him with rods. Ge said sternly: "Jiang Ge is sixty years old. Unable to give my life to repay my lord, today to die would be fortune enough. I swear I will not write at another's command."
translations.idiomatic: Yanming was about to beat him with rods. Ge said sternly, "Jiang Ge is sixty years old. Unable to give my life to repay my lord, to die today would be fortune enough. I swear I will not write at another's command."

sentences.zh: 延明知不可屈乃止。

translations.literal: Yanming knew he could not be bent and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming knew he could not be bent and stopped.

sentences.zh: 日給脫粟三升，僅餘性命。

translations.literal: Each day he was given three sheng of husked millet, barely enough to preserve life.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he was given three sheng of husked millet, barely enough to keep him alive.

sentences.zh: 會魏帝請中山王元略反北，乃放革及祖搄還朝。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor requested Prince Yuan Lue of Zhongshan to return north, he then released Ge and Zu Chong to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor requested Prince Yuan Lue of Zhongshan to return north, he released Ge and Zu Chong to return to court.

sentences.zh: 上大宴，舉酒勸革曰：「卿那不畏延明害？」

translations.literal: The emperor held a great banquet and raised his cup to urge Ge, saying: "Were you not afraid Yanming would harm you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held a great banquet and raised his cup to Ge, saying, "Were you not afraid Yanming would harm you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣行年六十，死不為夭，豈畏延明。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant is sixty years old; to die is not premature death—why fear Yanming."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your servant is sixty years old; to die is not premature death—why should I fear Yanming."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今日始見蘇武之節。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Today I first see the integrity of Su Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Today I first see the integrity of Su Wu."

sentences.zh: 於是以為太尉臨川王長史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, Prince Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was appointed chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, Prince Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 時帝惑於佛教，朝賢多啟求受戒。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was enamored of Buddhism; many court worthies petitioned to receive precepts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was enamored of Buddhism, and many court worthies petitioned to receive precepts.

sentences.zh: 革精信因果，而帝未知，謂革不奉佛法，乃賜革覺意詩五百字，云：「唯當勤精進，自強行勝修，豈可作底突，如彼必死囚。

translations.literal: Ge deeply believed in cause and effect, but the emperor did not know this and thought Ge did not follow Buddhist law. He therefore granted Ge a five-hundred-character poem on awakening intent, saying: "Only diligence and progress; strengthen yourself and practice what surpasses cultivation. How can one be a bottom bumpkin, like those condemned prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Ge deeply believed in cause and effect, but the emperor did not know this and thought Ge did not follow Buddhist teachings. He therefore granted Ge a five-hundred-character poem on awakening intent, saying, "Only diligence and progress; strengthen yourself and practice what surpasses cultivation. How can one be a stubborn fool, like those condemned prisoners.

sentences.zh: 以此告江革，並及諸貴遊。」

translations.literal: With this he informed Jiang Ge, and also the various noble travelers."
translations.idiomatic: With this he informed Jiang Ge, and also the various noble travelers."

sentences.zh: 又手敕曰：「果報不可不信，豈得底突如對元延明邪。」

translations.literal: He also wrote a personal edict: "Retribution cannot be disbelieved. How can one be a bottom bumpkin, like when facing Yuan Yanming."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a personal edict, "Retribution cannot be disbelieved. How can one be a stubborn fool, like when facing Yuan Yanming."

sentences.zh: 革因乞受菩薩戒。

translations.literal: Ge therefore petitioned to receive the bodhisattva precepts.
translations.idiomatic: Ge therefore petitioned to receive the bodhisattva precepts.

sentences.zh: 時武陵王紀在東州，頗驕縱，上以臧盾性弱，不能匡正，召革慰遣，乃除武陵王長史、會稽郡丞，行府州事。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Wuling Ji was in the eastern province, rather arrogant and unrestrained. The emperor, thinking Zang Dun's nature weak and unable to correct him, summoned Ge to comfort and dispatch him, then appointed him chief clerk to Prince Wuling, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery, and acting prefectural and provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Wuling Ji was in the eastern province, rather arrogant and unrestrained. The emperor, thinking Zang Dun's nature too weak to correct him, summoned Ge and dispatched him to the post of chief clerk to Prince Wuling, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery, and acting prefectural and provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 革門生故吏家多在東，聞革應至，並賚持緣道迎候。

translations.literal: Many of Ge's disciples and former subordinates had homes in the east; hearing Ge was coming, they all brought gifts and waited along the road to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Ge's disciples and former subordinates had homes in the east. Hearing that Ge was coming, they all brought gifts and waited along the road to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 革曰：「我通不受餉，不容獨當故人筐篚。」

translations.literal: Ge said: "I have never accepted gifts; I cannot alone receive my old friends' baskets and boxes."
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "I have never accepted gifts; I cannot alone receive my old friends' baskets and boxes."

sentences.zh: 至鎮唯資公俸，食不兼味。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post he relied only on official salary; his meals had no second dish.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his post he relied only on his official salary and ate no more than one dish at a meal.

sentences.zh: 郡境殷廣，辭訟日數百，革分判辯析，曾無疑滯，人安吏畏，百城震恐。

translations.literal: The commandery's territory was broad and populous; lawsuits numbered hundreds each day. Ge divided, judged, and analyzed them without ever hesitating. The people were at peace and the clerks feared him; the hundred cities trembled in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery's territory was broad and populous, with hundreds of lawsuits each day. Ge divided, judged, and analyzed them without hesitation. The people were at peace, the clerks feared him, and the hundred cities trembled in awe.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王騫為山陰令，贓貨狼籍，望風自解。

translations.literal: Prince Qian of Langya served as magistrate of Shanyin, his ill-gotten goods scattered everywhere; at the news he resigned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qian of Langya served as magistrate of Shanyin, his ill-gotten goods scattered everywhere. At the news of Ge's arrival he resigned of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 府王憚之。

translations.literal: The prince of the domain feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of the domain feared him.

sentences.zh: 每侍燕，言論必以詩、書，王因此耽學好文。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, his discourse always drew on the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents; because of this the prince became devoted to study and fond of literature.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended banquets, his discourse always drew on the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents. Because of this the prince became devoted to study and fond of literature.

sentences.zh: 典簽沈熾文以王所制詩呈武帝，帝謂僕射徐勉曰：「革果稱職。」

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Ge truly fills his post."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian, "Ge truly fills his post."

sentences.zh: 乃除都官尚書。

translations.literal: He then appointed him Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed him Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 將還，贈遺一無所受，送故依舊訂舫，革並不納，唯乘台所給一舸。

translations.literal: When about to return, he accepted no gifts whatsoever. The farewell escort arranged boats as usual, but Ge accepted none and took only the single skiff provided by the administration.
translations.idiomatic: When about to return, he accepted no gifts whatsoever. The farewell escort arranged boats as usual, but Ge accepted none and took only the single skiff provided by the administration.

sentences.zh: 舸艚偏欹，不得安臥。

translations.literal: The skiff listed to one side and he could not lie down in comfort.
translations.idiomatic: The skiff listed to one side and he could not lie down in comfort.

sentences.zh: 或請濟江徙重物以迮輕艚，革既無物，乃於西陵岸取石十餘片以實之。

translations.literal: Someone suggested crossing the river and moving heavy objects to ballast the light skiff. Ge had no possessions, so he took more than ten stones from the bank at Xiling to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone suggested crossing the river and moving heavy objects to ballast the light skiff. Ge had no possessions, so he took more than ten stones from the bank at Xiling to fill it.

sentences.zh: 其清貧如此。

translations.literal: Such was his purity and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his purity and poverty.

sentences.zh: 尋監吳郡，時境內荒儉，劫盜公行。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised Wu Commandery. At the time the territory within was stricken by famine, and bandits and robbers operated openly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he supervised Wu Commandery. At the time the territory was stricken by famine, and bandits and robbers operated openly.

sentences.zh: 革至郡唯有公給仗身二十人，百姓皆懼不能靜寇，革反省游軍尉，百姓逾恐。

translations.literal: When Ge arrived at the commandery he had only twenty armed attendants provided by the administration. The common people all feared he could not pacify the bandits. Ge then dismissed the touring army commandant, and the people grew even more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge arrived at the commandery he had only twenty armed attendants provided by the administration. The common people feared he could not pacify the bandits. Ge then dismissed the touring army commandant, and the people grew even more afraid.

sentences.zh: 革乃廣施恩惠，盜賊靜息。

translations.literal: Ge then broadly dispensed kindness and favor, and the bandits and robbers quieted.
translations.idiomatic: Ge then broadly dispensed kindness and favor, and the bandits and robbers quieted.

sentences.zh: 武陵王出鎮江州，乃曰：「我得江革文，得革清貧，豈能一日忘之，當與其同飽。」

translations.literal: When Prince Wuling went out to command Jiangzhou, he said: "I have gained Jiang Ge's writing and gained Ge's purity and poverty—how can I forget this for a single day? I shall share fullness with him."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wuling went out to command Jiangzhou, he said, "I have gained Jiang Ge's writing and gained Ge's purity and poverty—how can I forget this for a single day? I shall share my table with him."

sentences.zh: 乃表革同行。

translations.literal: He then memorialized requesting Ge to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized requesting Ge to accompany him.
