sentences.zh: 除南中郎長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: Ge was appointed chief clerk of the Southern Palace Guard and Administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was appointed chief clerk of the Southern Palace Guard and Administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 征入為度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 好獎進閭閻，為後生延譽，由是衣冠士子翕然歸之。

translations.literal: He loved to encourage and advance men of the lanes and wards, extending reputation for younger generations; thereby gentry and scholars converged upon him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to encourage and advance men of the lanes and wards, extending reputation for younger generations. Thereby gentry and scholars converged upon him.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令何敬容掌選，序用多非其人。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong managed selection, and many of those he appointed in order were not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong managed selection, and many of those he appointed were not the right men.

sentences.zh: 革性強直，每朝宴恒有褒貶，以此為權貴所疾。

translations.literal: Ge's nature was forceful and upright; at every court banquet he always had praise and blame, and for this was resented by the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Ge's nature was forceful and upright. At every court banquet he always had praise and blame to offer, and for this the powerful and noble resented him.

sentences.zh: 乃謝病還家，除光祿大夫，優遊閑放，以文酒自娛。

translations.literal: He then pleaded illness and returned home, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and lived at leisure in ease, finding pleasure in literature and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness and returned home. Appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, he lived at leisure and found pleasure in literature and wine.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰強子。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Qiangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was given the posthumous name Qiangzi.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works of twenty scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works of twenty scrolls circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 革曆官八府長史，四王行事，三為二千石，傍無姬侍，家徒壁立，時以此高之。

translations.literal: Ge successively served as chief clerk in eight princely administrations, acted in affairs for four princes, three times held the rank of two-thousand-dan official, had no concubines at his side, and his household was bare as walls; the age honored him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Ge successively served as chief clerk in eight princely administrations, acted in affairs for four princes, and three times held the rank of two-thousand-dan official. He had no concubines at his side and his household was bare as walls; the age honored him for this.

sentences.zh: 長子行敏早卒，次子德藻。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingmin died early; his second son was Dezao.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xingmin died early; his second son was Dezao.

sentences.zh: 德藻字德藻，好學，美風儀，身長七尺四寸。

translations.literal: Dezao, styled Dezao, loved learning, had fine bearing, and stood seven feet four inches tall.
translations.idiomatic: Dezao, styled Dezao, loved learning, had fine bearing, and stood seven feet four inches tall.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，事親盡禮。

translations.literal: His nature was supremely filial; in serving his parents he fulfilled every rite.
translations.idiomatic: Supremely filial by nature, he served his parents with complete devotion to ritual.

sentences.zh: 與異產昆弟居，恩惠甚篤。

translations.literal: He lived with half-brothers of different mothers, and his kindness was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with half-brothers of different mothers and treated them with deep kindness.

sentences.zh: 涉獵經籍，善屬文。

translations.literal: He ranged through the classics and was skilled at composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through the classics and was skilled at composing prose.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為尚書比部郎，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Director of the Comparison Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Liang as Director of the Comparison Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat and left office on his father's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋後，容貌毀瘠，如居喪時。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, his appearance was wasted and gaunt, as though still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, his appearance remained wasted and gaunt, as though still in mourning.

sentences.zh: 及陳武帝受禪，為秘書監，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen accepted the abdication, he became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen accepted the abdication, he became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon, in his existing post, he additionally served as Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, in his existing post, he additionally served as Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，兼散騎常侍，與中書郎劉師知使齊，著北征道里記三卷。

translations.literal: In the Tianjia era, he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and, with Director of the Secretariat Liu Shizhi, was envoy to Qi, composing the Record of Routes on the Northern Expedition in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjia era, he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and, with Director of the Secretariat Liu Shizhi, was envoy to Qi, composing the Record of Routes on the Northern Expedition in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 還除太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Upon return he was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，坐公事免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and was dismissed for an official matter.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and was dismissed for an official matter.

sentences.zh: 後自求宰縣，補新渝令。

translations.literal: Later he himself requested to govern a county and was appointed magistrate of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he himself requested to govern a county and was appointed magistrate of Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 政尚恩惠，頗有異績。

translations.literal: His governance prized kindness and favor and achieved notable results.
translations.idiomatic: His governance prized kindness and favor and achieved notable results.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，文帝贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died in office; Emperor Wen posthumously granted him Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; Emperor Wen posthumously granted him the rank of Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 文筆十五卷。

translations.literal: His literary writings filled fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His literary writings filled fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子椿亦善屬文，位尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His son Chun was also skilled at composing prose and held the post of Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun was also skilled at composing prose and served as Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德藻弟從簡，少有文情，年十七，作采荷調以刺何敬容，為當時所賞。

translations.literal: Dezao's younger brother Congjian had literary talent from youth. At seventeen he composed the Tune of Picking Lotus to satirize He Jingrong and was admired by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Dezao's younger brother Congjian had literary talent from youth. At seventeen he composed the Tune of Picking Lotus to satirize He Jingrong and was admired by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 位司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Attendant of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，為任約所害。

translations.literal: During the Hou Jing rebellion he was killed by Ren Yue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hou Jing rebellion he was killed by Ren Yue.

sentences.zh: 子兼叩

translations.literal: His son Jian knocked
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian knocked

sentences.zh: 頭流血，乞代父命，以身蔽刃，遂俱見殺，天下痛之。

translations.literal: his head until it bled, begging to take his father's place, shielding the blade with his body; in the end both were killed, and the empire grieved for them.
translations.idiomatic: his head until it bled, begging to take his father's place and shielding the blade with his body. In the end both were killed, and the empire grieved for them.

sentences.zh: 徐勉字修仁，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Mian, styled Xiuren, was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian, styled Xiuren, was a native of Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 祖長宗，宋武帝霸府行參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Changzong was Acting Military Affairs Aide in Emperor Wu of Song's hegemonic administration.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Changzong served as Acting Military Affairs Aide in Emperor Wu of Song's hegemonic administration.

sentences.zh: 父融，南昌相。

translations.literal: His father Rong was Chancellor of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong served as Chancellor of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 勉幼孤貧，早勵清節。

translations.literal: Mian was orphaned young and poor, and early cultivated purity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was orphaned young and poor, and early cultivated purity of conduct.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，屬霖雨，家人祈霽，率爾為文，見稱耆宿。

translations.literal: At six, during prolonged rain, when the family prayed for clear skies, he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.
translations.idiomatic: At six, during prolonged rain, when the family prayed for clear skies, he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.

sentences.zh: 及長好學，宗人孝嗣見之歎曰：「此所謂人中之騏驥，必能致千里。」

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning. His clansman Xiaosi saw him and sighed, saying: "This is what they call a thoroughbred among men—he will surely reach a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: When grown he loved learning. His clansman Xiaosi saw him and sighed, saying, "This is what they call a thoroughbred among men—he will surely reach a thousand li."

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂諸子曰：「此人師也，爾等則而行之。」

translations.literal: He also once told his sons: "This man is a teacher; you should take him as your model and follow him."
translations.idiomatic: He also once told his sons, "This man is a teacher; you should take him as your model and follow him."

sentences.zh: 年十八，召為國子生，便下帷專學，精力無怠。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was summoned as a student of the National University, drew the curtain and devoted himself to study, his energy never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was summoned as a student of the National University, drew the curtain and devoted himself to study, his energy never slackening.

sentences.zh: 同時儕輩肅而敬之。

translations.literal: Contemporaries of the same generation were solemn and respectful toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries of the same generation were solemn and respectful toward him.

sentences.zh: 祭酒王儉每見，常目送之，曰：「此子非常器也。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Wang Jian whenever he saw him would gaze after him and say: "This youth is no ordinary vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Jian whenever he saw him would gaze after him and say, "This youth is no ordinary vessel."

sentences.zh: 每稱有宰輔之量。

translations.literal: He often declared that Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: He often declared that Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 射策甲科，起家王國侍郎，補太學博士。

translations.literal: In the archery-and-policy examination he ranked in the top class. He began his career as Gentleman of a princely domain and was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the archery-and-policy examination he ranked in the top class. He began his career as Gentleman of a princely domain and was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時每有議定，勉理證明允，莫能貶奪，同官咸取則焉。

translations.literal: Whenever there was deliberation and decision at the time, Mian's reasoning was clear and fair; none could diminish or overturn it, and colleagues all took him as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was deliberation and decision at the time, Mian's reasoning was clear and fair. None could diminish or overturn it, and colleagues all took him as their standard.

sentences.zh: 遷臨海王西中郎田曹行參軍，俄徙署都曹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Western Palace Guard under Prince Linhai, and soon moved to serve in the Capital Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Western Palace Guard under Prince Linhai, and soon moved to serve in the Capital Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時琅邪王融一時才俊，特相慕悅，嘗請交焉。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Rong of Langya was a leading talent of the age and especially admired and delighted in him, once requesting friendship.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Rong of Langya was a leading talent of the age and especially admired him, once requesting friendship.

sentences.zh: 勉謂所親曰：「王郎名高望促，難可輕霹衣裾。」

translations.literal: Mian said to those close to him: "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one cannot lightly attach oneself to his hem."
translations.idiomatic: Mian said to those close to him, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one cannot lightly attach oneself to his hem."

sentences.zh: 融後果陷於法，以此見推識鑒。

translations.literal: Rong later indeed fell afoul of the law; for this Mian was praised for his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Rong later indeed fell afoul of the law; for this Mian was praised for his discernment.

sentences.zh: 累遷領軍長史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the Army of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the Army of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 初與長沙宣武王游，梁武帝深器賞之，及武帝兵至建鄴，勉于新林謁見，帝甚加恩禮，使管書記。

translations.literal: Early on he associated with Prince Xuanwu of Changsha; Emperor Wu of Liang deeply valued and admired him. When the emperor's army reached Jiankang, Mian paid his respects at Xinlin; the emperor greatly added favor and courtesy and had him manage records.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he associated with Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, and Emperor Wu of Liang deeply valued him. When the emperor's army reached Jiankang, Mian paid his respects at Xinlin. The emperor greatly honored him and had him manage records.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，拜中書侍郎，進領中書通事舍人，直內省。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, Mian was appointed Director of the Secretariat, then advanced to General Affairs Attendant of the Secretariat, serving in the inner office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, Mian was appointed Director of the Secretariat, then advanced to General Affairs Attendant of the Secretariat, serving in the inner office.

sentences.zh: 遷臨川王后軍諮議、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Affairs Counselor to the Rear Army of Prince Linchuan and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Affairs Counselor to the Rear Army of Prince Linchuan and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自掌樞憲，多所糾舉，時論以為稱職。

translations.literal: From managing the pivot of law and censure he impeached many; public opinion considered him fit for his post.
translations.idiomatic: From managing the pivot of law and censure he impeached many; public opinion considered him fit for his post.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，除給事黃門侍郎，尚書吏部郎，參掌大選。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian, he was appointed Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Director of the Personnel Bureau, and took part in managing the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianjian, he was appointed Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Director of the Personnel Bureau, and took part in managing the great selection of officials.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時師方侵魏，候驛填委。

translations.literal: At the time the army was invading Wei, and courier stations were piled with dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the army was invading Wei, and courier stations were piled with dispatches.

sentences.zh: 勉參掌軍書，劬勞夙夜，動經數旬，乃一還家。

translations.literal: Mian took part in managing military documents, toiling early and late; often several tens of days would pass before he returned home once.
translations.idiomatic: Mian took part in managing military documents, toiling early and late. Often several tens of days would pass before he returned home once.

sentences.zh: 群犬驚吠，勉歎曰：「吾憂國忘家，乃至於此。

translations.literal: The household dogs barked in alarm. Mian sighed and said: "I worry for the state and forget my home, even to this point.
translations.idiomatic: The household dogs barked in alarm. Mian sighed and said, "I worry for the state and forget my home, even to this point.

sentences.zh: 若吾亡後，亦是傳中一事。」

translations.literal: If after my death this too will be an item in my biography."
translations.idiomatic: If after my death this too will be an item in my biography."

sentences.zh: 六年，除給事中、五兵尚書，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Supervisor of Attendants and Minister of War, then transferred to Minister of the Personnel Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Supervisor of Attendants and Minister of War, then transferred to Minister of the Personnel Bureau.

sentences.zh: 勉居選官，彝倫有序。

translations.literal: Mian held the post of selection officer, and human relations were ordered.
translations.idiomatic: As selection officer, Mian brought order to human relations and appointments.

sentences.zh: 既閑尺牘，兼善辭令，雖文案填積，坐客充滿，應對如流，手不停筆。

translations.literal: Skilled both in documents and in eloquence, though papers piled up and seated guests filled the room, he responded like flowing water, his hand never stopping the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled both in documents and in eloquence, though papers piled up and seated guests filled the room, he responded like flowing water, his hand never stopping the brush.

sentences.zh: 又該綜百氏，皆避其諱。

translations.literal: He also mastered the hundred clans, and all avoided his taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: He also mastered the genealogies of the hundred clans, and all avoided his taboo name.

sentences.zh: 嘗及閘人夜集，客有虞暠求詹事五官。

translations.literal: Once, gathering at night with the gatekeeper, a guest named Yu Gao requested the five offices of the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Once, gathering at night with the gatekeeper, a guest named Yu Gao requested the five offices of the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 勉正色答云：「今夕止可談風月，不宜及公事。」

translations.literal: Mian answered with stern countenance: "Tonight one may speak only of wind and moon; public business is not suitable."
translations.idiomatic: Mian answered with stern countenance, "Tonight one may speak only of wind and moon; public business is not suitable."

sentences.zh: 故時人服其無私。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time admired his lack of partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore people of the time admired his lack of partiality.

sentences.zh: 天監初，官名互有省置，勉撰立選簿奏之，有詔施用。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, official titles were variously reduced and established. Mian drafted and submitted a selection register; an edict ordered its use.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian, official titles were variously reduced and established. Mian drafted and submitted a selection register, and an edict ordered its use.

sentences.zh: 其制開九品為十八班，自是貪冒苟進者以財貨取通，守道淪退者以貧寒見沒矣。

translations.literal: The system opened the nine ranks into eighteen grades. From then on, the greedy and rash in advancement obtained passage through wealth, while those who upheld the Way and sank into obscurity were submerged through poverty.
translations.idiomatic: The system opened the nine ranks into eighteen grades. From then on, the greedy and rash in advancement obtained passage through wealth, while those who upheld the Way and sank into obscurity were submerged through poverty.

sentences.zh: 後為左衛將軍，領太子中庶子，侍東宮。

translations.literal: Later he served as General of the Left Guard, concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, attending the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as General of the Left Guard, concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, attending the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子尚幼，敕知宮事，太子禮之甚重，每事詢謀。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming was still young; by edict Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs. The crown prince honored him greatly and consulted him on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming was still young. By edict Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs. The crown prince honored him greatly and consulted him on every matter.

sentences.zh: 嘗於殿講孝經，臨川王宏、尚書令沈約備二傅，勉與國子祭酒張充為執經，王瑩、張稷、柳憕、王暕為侍講。

translations.literal: Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.

sentences.zh: 時選極親賢，妙盡人譽。

translations.literal: The selection at the time was of the closest kin and worthiest men, wonderfully exhausting human praise.
translations.idiomatic: The selection at the time drew on the closest kin and worthiest men, winning universal praise.

sentences.zh: 勉陳讓數四，又與沈約書，求換侍講，詔弗許，然後就焉。

translations.literal: Mian declined several times, then wrote to Shen Yue requesting to exchange for lecture attendant; an edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Mian declined several times, then wrote to Shen Yue requesting to exchange for lecture attendant. An edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.

sentences.zh: 舊揚、徐首迎主簿，盡選國華中正，取勉子崧充南徐選首。

translations.literal: By old custom the chief clerks who welcomed the prince in Yang and Xu were all selected from the finest men of the state; Mian's son Song was chosen to fill the South Xu selection chief.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom the chief clerks who welcomed the prince in Yang and Xu were all selected from the finest men of the state. Mian's son Song was chosen to fill the South Xu selection chief.

sentences.zh: 帝敕之曰：「卿寒士，而子與王志子同迎，偃王以來未之有也。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "You are a humble scholar, yet your son welcomes the prince together with Wang Zhi's son—since King Yan there has been nothing like it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed him, "You are a humble scholar, yet your son welcomes the prince together with Wang Zhi's son—since King Yan there has been nothing like it."

sentences.zh: 勉恥以其先為戲，答旨不恭，由是左遷散騎常侍，領遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Mian was ashamed that his ancestors were made a jest; his reply to the edict was disrespectful, and for this he was demoted to Regular Attendant and concurrently General of the Mobile Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was ashamed that his ancestors were made a jest. His reply to the edict was disrespectful, and for this he was demoted to Regular Attendant and concurrently General of the Mobile Corps.

sentences.zh: 後為太子詹事，又遷尚書右僕射，詹事如故。

translations.literal: Later he served as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, then was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, his post as Supervisor remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, then was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, retaining his post as Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 時人間喪事多不遵禮，朝終夕殯，相尚以速。

translations.literal: At the time funerals among the people often did not follow ritual; mourning ended in the morning and encoffining came in the evening, with speed mutually prized.
translations.idiomatic: At the time funerals among the people often did not follow ritual. Mourning ended in the morning and encoffining came in the evening, with speed mutually prized.

sentences.zh: 勉上疏曰：「禮記問喪云：'三日而後斂者，以俟其生也。

translations.literal: Mian submitted a memorial saying: "The Record of Rites on questioning mourning says: 'Encoffining after three days is to await revival.
translations.idiomatic: Mian submitted a memorial saying, "The Record of Rites on questioning mourning says, ‘Encoffining after three days is to await revival.

sentences.zh: 三日而不生，亦不生矣。

translations.literal: If after three days there is no revival, there will be no revival.’
translations.idiomatic: If after three days there is no revival, there will be no revival.’

sentences.zh: '頃來不遵斯制，送終之禮，殯以期日。

translations.literal: Recently this system has not been followed; the rites of sending off the dead fix encoffining to a set day.
translations.idiomatic: Recently this system has not been followed; the rites of sending off the dead fix encoffining to a set day.

sentences.zh: 潤屋豪家，乃或半晷。

translations.literal: Wealthy houses that adorn their roofs sometimes do it in half a day.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy houses that adorn their roofs sometimes do it in half a day.

sentences.zh: 衣衾棺槨，以速為榮。

translations.literal: Garments, covers, coffins, and outer coffins take speed as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Garments, covers, coffins, and outer coffins take speed as glory.

sentences.zh: 親戚徒隸，各念休反。

translations.literal: Relatives and servants each think of rest and return.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and servants each think of rest and return.

sentences.zh: 故屬纊才畢，灰釘已具。

translations.literal: Therefore as soon as the final breath is taken, the lime and nails are already prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore as soon as the final breath is taken, the lime and nails are already prepared.

sentences.zh: 忘狐鼠之顧步，媿燕雀之徊翔，傷情滅理，莫此為大。

translations.literal: Forgetting the fox and rat's careful steps, ashamed before the swallow and sparrow's circling flight—injury to feeling and extinction of principle, nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Forgetting the fox and rat's careful steps, ashamed before the swallow and sparrow's circling flight—injury to feeling and extinction of principle, nothing is greater than this.

sentences.zh: 且人子承衾之時，志懣心絕，喪事所資，悉關他手。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a son receives the coverlet, his will is stifled and his heart cut off; all that supports the funeral depends on other hands.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when a son receives the coverlet, his will is stifled and his heart cut off. All that supports the funeral depends on other hands.

sentences.zh: 愛憎深淺，事實難原。

translations.literal: The depth of love and hate is hard to trace to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The depth of love and hate is hard to trace to the facts.

sentences.zh: 如覘視或爽，存沒違濫，使萬有其一，怨酷已多，豈若緩其告斂之辰，申其望生之冀。

translations.literal: If observation is in error, or the living and dead are treated with improper excess, even if only one in ten thousand, the grievous resentment is already great. How much better to slow the day of announcing encoffining and extend the hope for revival.
translations.idiomatic: If observation is in error, or the living and dead are treated with improper excess, even if only one in ten thousand, the grievous resentment is already great. How much better to slow the day of announcing encoffining and extend the hope for revival.

sentences.zh: 請自今士庶宜悉依古，三日大斂。

translations.literal: I request that from now on gentry and commoners should all follow antiquity and observe the three-day great encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: I request that from now on gentry and commoners should all follow antiquity and observe the three-day great encoffining.

sentences.zh: 如其不奉，加以糾繩。」

translations.literal: If they do not comply, add correction and discipline."
translations.idiomatic: If they do not comply, add correction and discipline."

sentences.zh: 詔可其奏。

translations.literal: An edict approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 又除尚書僕射、中衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 勉以舊恩，繼升重位，盡心奉上，知無不為。

translations.literal: Mian, through old favor, rose in succession to heavy posts, devoting his heart in serving the sovereign, doing all he knew to do.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, through old favor, rose in succession to heavy posts, devoting his heart to serving the sovereign and doing all he knew to do.

sentences.zh: 爰自小選迄於此職，常參掌衡石，甚得士心。

translations.literal: From minor selection up to this post, he always took part in managing the scales and weights, and greatly won the hearts of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: From minor selection up to this post, he always took part in managing appointments, and greatly won the hearts of scholars.

sentences.zh: 禁省中事，未嘗漏泄，每有表奏，輒焚稿草。

translations.literal: Affairs within the forbidden precincts he never leaked; whenever he submitted a memorial, he burned the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs within the forbidden precincts he never leaked. Whenever he submitted a memorial, he burned the draft.

sentences.zh: 博通經史，多識前載。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in the classics and histories, he knew much of earlier records.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly versed in the classics and histories, he knew much of earlier records.

sentences.zh: 齊世王儉居職已後，莫有逮者。

translations.literal: Since Wang Jian's tenure under Qi, none has matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Jian's tenure under Qi, none has matched him.

sentences.zh: 朝儀國典，昏冠吉凶，勉皆預圖議。

translations.literal: Court ritual, state statutes, capping and marriage, auspicious and inauspicious affairs—Mian all took part in planning and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual, state statutes, capping and marriage, auspicious and inauspicious affairs—Mian all took part in planning and deliberation.

sentences.zh: 初，勉受詔知撰五禮，普通六年功畢，表上之曰：

translations.literal: Earlier, Mian received an edict to oversee the compilation of the Five Rites. In the sixth year of Putong the work was completed, and he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Mian received an edict to oversee the compilation of the Five Rites. In the sixth year of Putong the work was completed, and he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 夫禮以安上化人，弘風訓俗，經國家，利後嗣者也。

translations.literal: Ritual is what settles superiors and transforms people, expands custom and instructs the folk, governs the state, and benefits posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is what settles superiors and transforms people, expands custom and instructs the folk, governs the state, and benefits posterity.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞、三代，咸必由之。

translations.literal: Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties all necessarily passed through it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties all necessarily passed through it.

sentences.zh: 在乎有周，憲章尤備，因殷革夏，損益可知。

translations.literal: In the Zhou, statutes and regulations were especially complete; following Yin in reforming Xia, additions and subtractions can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou, statutes and regulations were especially complete. Following Yin in reforming Xia, additions and subtractions can be known.

sentences.zh: 雖復經禮三百，曲禮三千，經文三百，威儀三千，其大歸有五，即宗伯所掌典禮，吉為上，凶次之，賓次之，軍次之，嘉為下也。

translations.literal: Though there were three hundred canonical rites, three thousand detailed rites, three hundred canonical texts, and three thousand ceremonial forms, their great categories are five: namely the canonical rites managed by the Minister of Rites—auspicious first, inauspicious second, guest third, military fourth, and celebratory last.
translations.idiomatic: Though there were three hundred canonical rites, three thousand detailed rites, three hundred canonical texts, and three thousand ceremonial forms, their great categories are five: namely the canonical rites managed by the Minister of Rites—auspicious first, inauspicious second, guest third, military fourth, and celebratory last.

sentences.zh: 故祠祭不以禮，則不齊不莊；

translations.literal: Therefore if sacrifice and offering are not by ritual, there is neither order nor dignity;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore if sacrifice and offering are not by ritual, there is neither order nor dignity;

sentences.zh: 喪紀不以禮，則背死忘生者眾；

translations.literal: if mourning regulations are not by ritual, many turn their backs on the dead and forget the living;
translations.idiomatic: if mourning regulations are not by ritual, many turn their backs on the dead and forget the living;

sentences.zh: 賓客不以禮，則朝覲失其儀；

translations.literal: if guests are not by ritual, court audiences lose their forms;
translations.idiomatic: if guests are not by ritual, court audiences lose their forms;

sentences.zh: 軍旅不以禮，則致亂于師律；

translations.literal: if armies are not by ritual, disorder arises in military law;
translations.idiomatic: if armies are not by ritual, disorder arises in military law;

sentences.zh: 冠昏不以禮，則男女失其時。

translations.literal: if capping and marriage are not by ritual, men and women miss their proper times.
translations.idiomatic: if capping and marriage are not by ritual, men and women miss their proper times.

sentences.zh: 為國修身，於斯攸急。

translations.literal: For governing the state and cultivating the person, in this it is urgently important.
translations.idiomatic: For governing the state and cultivating the person, in this it is urgently important.

sentences.zh: 洎周室大壞，王道既衰，官守斯文，日失其序。

translations.literal: When the Zhou house greatly collapsed and the royal way declined, officials guarding this culture daily lost its order.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou house greatly collapsed and the royal way declined, officials guarding this culture daily lost its order.

sentences.zh: 暴秦滅學，掃地無餘。

translations.literal: Violent Qin extinguished learning, sweeping the ground clean without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Violent Qin extinguished learning, sweeping the ground clean without remainder.

sentences.zh: 漢氏鬱興，日不暇給，猶命叔孫于外野，方知帝王之為貴。

translations.literal: Han flourished and rose; days allowed no respite, yet they still summoned Shusun in the outer wilds and then knew the nobility of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Han flourished and rose. Days allowed no respite, yet they still summoned Shusun in the outer wilds and then knew the nobility of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 末葉紛綸，遞有興毀。

translations.literal: In the late leaves it was tangled and confused, with rise and ruin in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the late period it was tangled and confused, with rise and ruin in succession.

sentences.zh: 及東京曹褒，南宮制述，集其散略，百有餘篇。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital Cao Bao and the Southern Palace made regulations and narratives, gathering scattered outlines into more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital Cao Bao and the Southern Palace made regulations and narratives, gathering scattered outlines into more than a hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 雖寫以尺簡，而終闕平奏。

translations.literal: Though written on foot-long slips, in the end the balanced memorial was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Though written on foot-long slips, in the end the balanced memorial was lacking.

sentences.zh: 其後兵革相尋，異端互起，章句既淪，俎豆斯輟。

translations.literal: Afterward arms and armor followed one upon another, heterodox teachings arose together, chapters and sentences sank away, and sacrificial vessels ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward arms and armor followed one upon another, heterodox teachings arose together, chapters and sentences sank away, and sacrificial vessels ceased.

sentences.zh: 方領矩步之容，事滅於旌鼓，蘭台石室之典，用盡于帷蓋。

translations.literal: The bearing of square collars and measured steps was extinguished by banners and drums; the statutes of the Orchid Terrace and Stone Chamber were exhausted in canopies and covers.
translations.idiomatic: The bearing of square collars and measured steps was extinguished by banners and drums; the statutes of the Orchid Terrace and Stone Chamber were exhausted in canopies and covers.

sentences.zh: 至乎晉氏，爰定新禮，荀顗制之於前，摯虞刪之於末。

translations.literal: As for the Jin house, they then fixed new rites: Xun Yi made them at the beginning, and Zhi Yu edited them at the end.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Jin house, they then fixed new rites: Xun Yi made them at the beginning, and Zhi Yu edited them at the end.

sentences.zh: 既而中原喪亂，罕有所遺，江左草創，因循而已。

translations.literal: Soon the central plains fell to chaos and little was preserved; the left bank of the Yangzi was newly founded and merely followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the central plains fell to chaos and little was preserved. The left bank of the Yangzi was newly founded and merely followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 厘革之風，是則未暇。

translations.literal: The wind of reform and change—there was then no leisure for it.
translations.idiomatic: The wind of reform and change—there was then no leisure for it.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下睿明啟運，先天改物，撥亂惟武，經俗以文。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty is wise and bright, opening the mandate, transforming things before Heaven, pacifying disorder through martial power and governing custom through culture.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty is wise and bright, opening the mandate, transforming things before Heaven, pacifying disorder through martial power and governing custom through culture.

sentences.zh: 作樂在乎功成，制禮弘於業定。

translations.literal: Making music lies in the completion of achievement; establishing ritual is grand when the enterprise is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Making music lies in the completion of achievement; establishing ritual is grand when the enterprise is settled.

sentences.zh: 伏尋所定五禮，起齊永明二年，太子步兵校尉伏曼容表求制一代禮樂。

translations.literal: I humbly trace the fixed Five Rites to the second year of Yongming under Qi, when Fu Manrong, Commandant of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent, memorialized requesting the making of ritual and music for one generation.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly trace the fixed Five Rites to the second year of Yongming under Qi, when Fu Manrong, Commandant of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent, memorialized requesting the making of ritual and music for one generation.

sentences.zh: 于時參議，置新舊學士十人，止修五禮，諮稟衛將軍丹陽尹王儉，學士亦分住郡中，製作歷年，猶未克就。

translations.literal: At the time in joint deliberation they established ten old and new scholars, limiting work to the Five Rites, consulting General of the Guard and Prefect of Danyang Wang Jian. The scholars also dispersed to live in commanderies. Production continued for years but was still not completed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time in joint deliberation they established ten old and new scholars, limiting work to the Five Rites and consulting General of the Guard and Prefect of Danyang Wang Jian. The scholars also dispersed to live in commanderies. Production continued for years but was still not completed.

sentences.zh: 及文憲薨，遺文散逸，又以事付國子祭酒何胤，經涉九載，猶復未畢。

translations.literal: When Wenxian died, surviving texts scattered and were lost. The task was again entrusted to Chancellor of the Imperial University He Yin; nine years passed, and it was still not finished.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxian died, surviving texts scattered and were lost. The task was again entrusted to Chancellor of the Imperial University He Yin. Nine years passed, and it was still not finished.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，胤還東山，齊明帝敕委尚書令徐孝嗣，舊事本末，隨在南第。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin returned to East Mountain. Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xiaosi take charge; the origins and ends of old affairs followed him to the southern residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin returned to East Mountain. Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xiaosi take charge. The origins and ends of old affairs followed him to the southern residence.

sentences.zh: 永元中，孝嗣於此遇禍，又多零落。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan, Xiaosi met disaster here, and much more was scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan, Xiaosi met disaster here, and much more was scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 當時鳩集所余，權付尚書左丞蔡仲熊、驍騎將軍何佟之共掌其事。

translations.literal: At the time what remained was gathered together and provisionally entrusted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Cai Zhongxiong and General of Valiant Cavalry He Tongzhi to manage the affair jointly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time what remained was gathered together and provisionally entrusted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Cai Zhongxiong and General of Valiant Cavalry He Tongzhi to manage the affair jointly.

sentences.zh: 時禮局住在國子學中門外，東昏之時，頻有軍火，其所散失，又踰太半。

translations.literal: At the time the Ritual Bureau dwelt outside the middle gate of the Imperial University. In the time of Donghun there were frequent military fires; what was scattered and lost exceeded half again.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Ritual Bureau dwelt outside the middle gate of the Imperial University. In the time of Donghun there were frequent military fires, and what was scattered and lost exceeded half again.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，佟之啟審省置之宜，敕使外詳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, Tongzhi memorialized examining whether abolition or retention was appropriate; an edict ordered detailed review outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian, Tongzhi memorialized examining whether abolition or retention was appropriate. An edict ordered detailed review outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 時尚書參詳，以天地初革，庶務權輿，宜俟隆平，徐議刪撰。

translations.literal: At the time the Imperial Secretariat jointly examined and held that Heaven and Earth had just been transformed, myriad affairs were in provisional rise, and one should await great peace before slowly deliberating deletion and compilation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Imperial Secretariat jointly examined and held that Heaven and Earth had just been transformed, myriad affairs were in provisional rise, and one should await great peace before slowly deliberating deletion and compilation.

sentences.zh: 欲且省禮局，並還尚書儀曹。

translations.literal: They wished for the time being to abolish the Ritual Bureau and return everything to the Ceremonial Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: They wished for the time being to abolish the Ritual Bureau and return everything to the Ceremonial Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔旨云：「禮壞樂缺，故國異家殊，實宜以時修定，以為永准。」

translations.literal: The edict's intent said: "Ritual is broken and music lacking, therefore states differ and families vary. It truly should be revised and fixed in season as an eternal standard."
translations.idiomatic: The edict's intent said, "Ritual is broken and music lacking, therefore states differ and families vary. It truly should be revised and fixed in season as an eternal standard."

sentences.zh: 於是尚書僕射沈約等參議，請五禮各置舊學士一人，人各自舉學士二人相助，抄撰其中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue and others jointly deliberated, requesting that each of the Five Rites have one old scholar appointed, each man recommending two scholars to assist, copying and compiling within them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue and others jointly deliberated, requesting that each of the Five Rites have one old scholar appointed, each man recommending two scholars to assist in copying and compiling.

sentences.zh: 有疑者依前漢石渠、後漢白虎，隨源以聞，請旨斷決。

translations.literal: Where there were doubts, following the Stone Canal of Former Han and the White Tiger of Later Han, trace the source and report, requesting imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Where there were doubts, following the Stone Canal of Former Han and the White Tiger of Later Han, trace the source and report, requesting imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 乃以舊學士右軍記室參軍明山賓掌吉禮，中軍騎兵參軍嚴植之掌凶禮，中軍田曹行參軍兼太常丞賀瑒掌賓禮，征虜記室參軍陸璉掌軍禮，右軍參軍事司馬褧掌嘉禮，尚書右丞何佟之總參其事。

translations.literal: They then appointed old scholar Ming Shanbin, Military Affairs Secretary of the Right Army, to manage auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Military Affairs Aide of the Central Army, to manage inauspicious rites; He Yang, Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Central Army and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies, to manage guest rites; Lu Lian, Military Affairs Secretary of the Campaign Against Barbarians, to manage military rites; Sima Jiong, Military Affairs Aide of the Right Army, to manage celebratory rites; and Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Tongzhi to oversee the affair in general.
translations.idiomatic: They then appointed old scholar Ming Shanbin, Military Affairs Secretary of the Right Army, to manage auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Military Affairs Aide of the Central Army, to manage inauspicious rites; He Yang, Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Central Army and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies, to manage guest rites; Lu Lian, Military Affairs Secretary of the Campaign Against Barbarians, to manage military rites; Sima Jiong, Military Affairs Aide of the Right Army, to manage celebratory rites; and Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Tongzhi to oversee the affair in general.

sentences.zh: 佟之亡後，以鎮北諮議參軍伏揯代之。

translations.literal: After Tongzhi died, Fu Yin, Military Affairs Counselor of Campaign North, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongzhi died, Fu Yin, Military Affairs Counselor of Campaign North, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 後又以揯代嚴植之掌凶禮。

translations.literal: Later Yin again replaced Yan Zhizhi in managing inauspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yin again replaced Yan Zhizhi in managing inauspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 揯尋遷官，以五經博士繆昭掌凶禮。

translations.literal: Yin soon moved to another post, and Miao Zhao, Erudite of the Five Classics, managed inauspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yin soon moved to another post, and Miao Zhao, Erudite of the Five Classics, managed inauspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 復以禮儀深廣，記載殘缺，宜須博論，共盡其致，更使鎮軍將軍丹陽尹沈約、太常卿張充及臣三人同參厥務，臣又奉別敕總知其事。

translations.literal: Again, because ritual propriety was deep and broad and records were fragmentary and incomplete, broad discussion was needed to exhaust its reach together. General of the Garrison Army and Prefect of Danyang Shen Yue, Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Chong, and your servant, three men, were further ordered to take part in the task jointly; your servant also received a separate edict to oversee the affair in general.
translations.idiomatic: Again, because ritual propriety was deep and broad and records were fragmentary and incomplete, broad discussion was needed to exhaust its reach together. General of the Garrison Army and Prefect of Danyang Shen Yue, Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Chong, and your servant, three men, were further ordered to take part in the task jointly. Your servant also received a separate edict to oversee the affair in general.

sentences.zh: 末又使中書侍郎周舍、庾於陵二人復豫參知。

translations.literal: Finally, Director of the Secretariat Zhou She and Yu Yuling, two men, were again ordered to take part in knowing the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Finally, Director of the Secretariat Zhou She and Yu Yuling, two men, were again ordered to take part in knowing the affair.

sentences.zh: 若有疑義，所掌學士當職先立議，通諮五禮舊學士及參知各言同異，條牒啟聞，決之制旨。

translations.literal: If there were doubtful points, the scholar in charge of the duty first established a proposal, consulted broadly with the old scholars of the Five Rites and those taking part in knowing, each stating agreement or difference, listed and reported upward, and decided by imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: If there were doubtful points, the scholar in charge first established a proposal, consulted broadly with the old scholars of the Five Rites and those taking part in knowing, each stating agreement or difference, listed and reported upward, and decided by imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 疑事既多，歲時又積，制旨裁斷，其數不少。

translations.literal: Doubtful matters were many and years accumulated; imperial decisions were not few in number.
translations.idiomatic: Doubtful matters were many and years accumulated; imperial decisions were not few in number.

sentences.zh: 莫不網羅經誥，玉振金聲。

translations.literal: None failed to net the classics and edicts, jade vibrating and gold sounding.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to net the classics and edicts, jade vibrating and gold sounding.

sentences.zh: 凡諸奏決，皆載篇首，具列聖旨，為不刊之則。

translations.literal: All memorial decisions were recorded at the head of each section, fully listing the sage's intent as an unalterable standard.
translations.idiomatic: All memorial decisions were recorded at the head of each section, fully listing the sage's intent as an unalterable standard.

sentences.zh: 甯孝宣之能擬，豈孝章之足云。

translations.literal: How can Ning Xiaoxuan's capacity be matched—can Emperor Xiaozhang even be mentioned?
translations.idiomatic: How can Ning Xiaoxuan's capacity be matched—can Emperor Xiaozhang even be mentioned?

sentences.zh: 五禮之職，事有繁簡，及其列畢，不得同時。

translations.literal: The duties of the Five Rites had affairs both complex and simple; when they were listed complete, they could not be finished at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: The duties of the Five Rites had affairs both complex and simple. When they were listed complete, they could not be finished at the same time.

sentences.zh: 嘉禮儀注以天監六年五月七日上尚書，合十有二帙，一百一十六卷，五百三十六條。

translations.literal: The ceremonial notes for celebratory rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the seventh day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling twelve fascicles, one hundred sixteen scrolls, and five hundred thirty-six articles.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial notes for celebratory rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the seventh day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling twelve fascicles, one hundred sixteen scrolls, and five hundred thirty-six articles.

sentences.zh: 賓禮儀注以天監六年五月二十日上尚書，合十有七帙，一百三十三卷，五百四十五條。

translations.literal: The ceremonial notes for guest rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the twentieth day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling seventeen fascicles, one hundred thirty-three scrolls, and five hundred forty-five articles.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial notes for guest rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the twentieth day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling seventeen fascicles, one hundred thirty-three scrolls, and five hundred forty-five articles.

sentences.zh: 軍禮儀注以天監九年十月二十九日上尚書，合十有八帙，一百八十九卷，二百四十條。

translations.literal: The ceremonial notes for military rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Tianjian, totaling eighteen fascicles, one hundred eighty-nine scrolls, and two hundred forty articles.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial notes for military rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Tianjian, totaling eighteen fascicles, one hundred eighty-nine scrolls, and two hundred forty articles.

sentences.zh: 吉禮儀注以天監十一年十一月十日上尚書，合二十有六帙，二百二十四卷，一千五條。

translations.literal: The ceremonial notes for auspicious rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling twenty-six fascicles, two hundred twenty-four scrolls, and one thousand five articles.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial notes for auspicious rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling twenty-six fascicles, two hundred twenty-four scrolls, and one thousand five articles.

sentences.zh: 凶禮儀注以天監十一年十一月十七日上尚書，合四十有七帙，五百一十四卷，五千六百九十三條。

translations.literal: The ceremonial notes for inauspicious rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling forty-seven fascicles, five hundred fourteen scrolls, and five thousand six hundred ninety-three articles.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial notes for inauspicious rites were submitted to the Imperial Secretariat on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling forty-seven fascicles, five hundred fourteen scrolls, and five thousand six hundred ninety-three articles.

sentences.zh: 大凡一百二十帙，一千一百七十六卷，八千一十九條。

translations.literal: In all, one hundred twenty fascicles, one thousand one hundred seventy-six scrolls, and eight thousand nineteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: In all, one hundred twenty fascicles, one thousand one hundred seventy-six scrolls, and eight thousand nineteen articles.

sentences.zh: 又列副秘閣及五經典書各一通，繕寫校定，以普通五年二月始獲洗畢。

translations.literal: Also listed were duplicate copies for the Secret Archive and one complete set each of the Five Classics, copied, written, collated, and fixed; only in the second month of the fifth year of Putong was the cleansing completed.
translations.idiomatic: Also listed were duplicate copies for the Secret Archive and one complete set each of the Five Classics, copied, written, collated, and fixed. Only in the second month of the fifth year of Putong was the cleansing completed.

sentences.zh: 竊以撰正履禮，歷代罕就，皇明在運，厥功克成。

translations.literal: I venture to hold that compiling and correcting and fulfilling ritual has rarely been achieved through the ages; the august brightness is in the mandate, and this merit has been able to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to hold that compiling and correcting and fulfilling ritual has rarely been achieved through the ages. The august brightness is in the mandate, and this merit has been able to succeed.

sentences.zh: 周代三千，舉其盈數，今之八千，隨事附益。

translations.literal: The Zhou had three thousand, taking its full number; today's eight thousand follows affairs in addition and increase.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou had three thousand, taking its full number. Today's eight thousand follows affairs in addition and increase.

sentences.zh: 質文相變，故其數兼倍，猶如八卦之爻，因而重之，錯綜成六十四也。

translations.literal: Substance and pattern change each other, therefore the number is doubled as well, just as the lines of the eight trigrams, thereby doubled and interwoven, become sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Substance and pattern change each other, therefore the number is doubled as well, just as the lines of the eight trigrams, thereby doubled and interwoven, become sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸識，謬司其任，淹留曆稔，允當斯責。

translations.literal: Your servant, with mediocre understanding, wrongly holds this post; lingering through accumulated years, I am indeed fit for this responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, with mediocre understanding, wrongly holds this post. Lingering through accumulated years, I am indeed fit for this responsibility.

sentences.zh: 兼勒成之初，未遑表上，實由才輕務廣，思力不周，永言慚惕，無忘寤寐。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of completion there was no leisure to submit upward; truly because talent was light and tasks broad, thought and strength were not complete. Speaking forever, I am ashamed and cautious, never forgetting waking or sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the beginning of completion there was no leisure to submit upward, truly because talent was light and tasks broad, thought and strength were not complete. I am forever ashamed and cautious, never forgetting waking or sleeping.

sentences.zh: 自今春輿駕將親六師，搜尋軍禮，閱其條章，靡不該備，可以懸諸日月，頒之天下者矣。

translations.literal: From this spring the imperial carriage will personally lead the Six Armies. Searching out military rites and reviewing their articles, none is not fully provided; it can be hung beside sun and moon and promulgated throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: From this spring the imperial carriage will personally lead the Six Armies. Searching out military rites and reviewing their articles, none is not fully provided. It can be hung beside sun and moon and promulgated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 詔有司案以遵行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to examine and follow it in practice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relevant offices to examine and follow it in practice.

sentences.zh: 尋加中書令，勉以疾求解內任，詔不許，乃令停下省，三日一朝，有事遣主書論決。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Director of the Secretariat. Mian, because of illness, requested release from inner duties; an edict did not permit it, but ordered him to stop at the lower office, attend court once every three days, and when there were matters send the chief clerk to discuss and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made Director of the Secretariat. Mian, because of illness, requested release from inner duties. An edict did not permit it, but ordered him to stop at the lower office, attend court once every three days, and when there were matters send the chief clerk to discuss and decide.

sentences.zh: 患腳轉劇，久闕朝覲，固陳求解，詔許疾差還省。

translations.literal: His foot ailment grew severe; long absent from court audience, he firmly memorialized requesting release. An edict permitted him to return to office when illness improved.
translations.idiomatic: His foot ailment grew severe. Long absent from court audience, he firmly memorialized requesting release. An edict permitted him to return to office when illness improved.

sentences.zh: 勉雖居顯職，不營產業，家無畜積，奉祿分贍親族之貧乏者。

translations.literal: Though Mian held an eminent post, he did not manage estates; the household had no stored wealth, and he divided his salary to support poor relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mian held an eminent post, he did not manage estates. The household had no stored wealth, and he divided his salary to support poor relatives.

sentences.zh: 門人故舊或從容致言，勉乃答曰：「人遺子孫以財，我遺之清白。

translations.literal: Disciples and old friends sometimes spoke at leisure; Mian then answered: "People bequeath wealth to descendants; I bequeath them purity.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples and old friends sometimes spoke at leisure. Mian then answered, "People bequeath wealth to descendants; I bequeath them purity.

sentences.zh: 子孫才也，則自致輜軿；

translations.literal: If descendants have talent, they will themselves obtain carriages and teams;
translations.idiomatic: If descendants have talent, they will themselves obtain carriages and teams;

sentences.zh: 如不才，終為佗有。」

translations.literal: if they lack talent, in the end it belongs to others."
translations.idiomatic: if they lack talent, in the end it belongs to others."

sentences.zh: 嘗為書戒其子崧曰：

translations.literal: He once wrote a letter admonishing his son Song, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a letter admonishing his son Song, saying:

sentences.zh: 吾家本清廉，故常居貧素。

translations.literal: Our family has always been pure and honest, therefore we constantly live in poverty and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Our family has always been pure and honest, therefore we constantly live in poverty and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 至於產業之事，所未嘗言，非直不經營而已。

translations.literal: As for matters of estates, I have never spoken of them—not merely that I do not manage them.
translations.idiomatic: As for matters of estates, I have never spoken of them—not merely that I do not manage them.

sentences.zh: 薄躬遭逢，遂至今日，尊官厚祿，可謂備之。

translations.literal: My slight person met with opportunity and reached today; eminent office and generous salary can be said to be complete.
translations.idiomatic: My slight person met with opportunity and reached today. Eminent office and generous salary can be said to be complete.

sentences.zh: 每念叨竊若斯，豈由才致，仰藉先門風範及以福慶，故臻此爾，古人所謂「以清白遺子孫，不亦厚乎？」。

translations.literal: Each time I think how I have undeservedly reached this, it is not by talent alone; relying on the bearing of former generations and on fortune and blessing, I therefore attained this. As the ancients said, "To bequeath purity to descendants—is that not generous?"
translations.idiomatic: Each time I think how I have undeservedly reached this, it is not by talent alone. Relying on the bearing of former generations and on fortune and blessing, I therefore attained this. As the ancients said, "To bequeath purity to descendants—is that not generous?"

sentences.zh: 又云：「遺子黃金滿籯，不如一經」。

translations.literal: They also said: "To bequeath a child gold filling a chest is not as good as one classic."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "To bequeath a child gold filling a chest is not as good as one classic."

sentences.zh: 詳求此言，信非徒語。

translations.literal: Examining this saying carefully, it is truly not empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Examining this saying carefully, it is truly not empty words.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不敏，實有本志，庶得遵奉斯義，不敢墜失。

translations.literal: Though I am not keen, I truly have this original intent, hoping to follow and uphold this principle and not dare to let it fall away.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not keen, I truly have this original intent, hoping to follow and uphold this principle and not dare to let it fall away.

sentences.zh: 所以顯貴以來，將三十載，門人故舊，承薦便宜，或使創辟田園，或勸興立邸店；

translations.literal: Therefore since becoming eminent and honored, for nearly thirty years, disciples and old friends, accepting recommendations of convenience, sometimes had me open up gardens and fields, or urged me to establish inns and shops;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore since becoming eminent and honored, for nearly thirty years, disciples and old friends, accepting recommendations of convenience, sometimes had me open up gardens and fields, or urged me to establish inns and shops;

sentences.zh: 又欲舳艫運致，亦令貨殖聚斂。

translations.literal: some also wished boats and ships to transport goods, likewise letting trade accumulate and gather.
translations.idiomatic: some also wished boats and ships to transport goods, likewise letting trade accumulate and gather.

sentences.zh: 若此眾事，皆距而不納。

translations.literal: Matters such as these I all rejected and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Matters such as these I all rejected and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 非謂拔葵去織，且欲省息紛紜。

translations.literal: This is not to say pulling up mallows and removing weaving, but rather wishing to reduce and quiet confusion.
translations.idiomatic: This is not to say pulling up mallows and removing weaving, but rather wishing to reduce and quiet confusion.

sentences.zh: 中年聊于東田開營小園者，非存播藝以要利，政欲穿池種樹，少寄情賞。

translations.literal: In middle age I casually opened and managed a small garden in the eastern field—not to preserve sowing and planting for profit, but simply wishing to dig a pond and plant trees, briefly lodging feeling and appreciation.
translations.idiomatic: In middle age I casually opened and managed a small garden in the eastern field—not to preserve sowing and planting for profit, but simply wishing to dig a pond and plant trees, briefly lodging feeling and appreciation.

sentences.zh: 又以郊際閑曠，終可為宅，儻獲懸車致事，實欲歌哭於斯。

translations.literal: Also because the suburban outskirts are open and spacious, in the end it can serve as a residence; if I should obtain suspension of the carriage and retirement from affairs, I truly wish to sing and weep here.
translations.idiomatic: Also because the suburban outskirts are open and spacious, in the end it can serve as a residence. If I should obtain suspension of the carriage and retirement from affairs, I truly wish to sing and weep here.

sentences.zh: 慧日、十住等既應營昏，又須住止。

translations.literal: Huiri, Shizhu, and others must both manage marriage and need lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Huiri, Shizhu, and others must both manage marriage and need lodging.

sentences.zh: 吾清明門宅無相容處，所以爾者，亦復有以。

translations.literal: My residence at Qingming Gate has no room to accommodate them; the reason for this also has its grounds.
translations.idiomatic: My residence at Qingming Gate has no room to accommodate them. The reason for this also has its grounds.

sentences.zh: 前割西邊施宣武寺，既失西廂，不復方幅，意亦謂此逆旅舍爾，何事須華。

translations.literal: Earlier the western side was cut off to endow Xuanwu Temple; having lost the western wing, it was no longer square and ample. I also considered this an inn or lodging—why need splendor?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the western side was cut off to endow Xuanwu Temple. Having lost the western wing, it was no longer square and ample. I also considered this an inn or lodging—why need splendor?

sentences.zh: 常恨時人謂是我宅。

translations.literal: I often resented that people of the time called it my residence.
translations.idiomatic: I often resented that people of the time called it my residence.

sentences.zh: 古往今來，豪富繼踵，高門甲第，連闥洞房，宛其死矣，定是誰室？

translations.literal: From ancient times to the present, the wealthy and powerful follow in succession—high gates and noble mansions, linked doors and inner chambers. When they die, whose rooms will these surely be?
translations.idiomatic: From ancient times to the present, the wealthy and powerful follow in succession—high gates and noble mansions, linked doors and inner chambers. When they die, whose rooms will these surely be?

sentences.zh: 但不能不為培塿之山，聚石移果，雜以花卉，以娛休沐，用托性靈。

translations.literal: Yet one cannot fail to make a hill of a mound, gather stones and transplant fruit, mix in flowers and plants, to amuse oneself on days of rest, and lodge one's nature and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one cannot fail to make a hill of a mound, gather stones and transplant fruit, mix in flowers and plants, to amuse oneself on days of rest, and lodge one's nature and spirit.

sentences.zh: 隨便架立，不存廣大，唯功德處小以為好，所以內中逼促，無復房宇。

translations.literal: Set up casually without aiming at grandeur, considering small merit halls best; therefore within it is cramped and there are no longer rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Set up casually without aiming at grandeur, considering small merit halls best. Therefore within it is cramped and there are no longer rooms.

sentences.zh: 近修東邊兒孫二宅，乃藉十住南還之資，其中所須，猶為不少。

translations.literal: Recently building the two residences of eastern descendants and grandchildren, I relied on the funds from Shizhu's return south; what was needed within was still not small.
translations.idiomatic: Recently building the two residences of eastern descendants and grandchildren, I relied on the funds from Shizhu's return south. What was needed within was still not small.

sentences.zh: 既牽挽不至，又不可中途而輟，郊間之園，遂不辦保，貨與韋黯，乃獲百金。

translations.literal: Since funds could not be drawn in time and one could not stop halfway, the suburban garden could not be kept; it was sold to Wei An, obtaining a hundred gold.
translations.idiomatic: Since funds could not be drawn in time and one could not stop halfway, the suburban garden could not be kept. It was sold to Wei An, obtaining a hundred gold.

sentences.zh: 成就兩宅，已消其半。

translations.literal: Completing the two residences already consumed half of it.
translations.idiomatic: Completing the two residences already consumed half of it.

sentences.zh: 尋園價所得，何以至此？

translations.literal: Searching how the garden's price could reach this—how did it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Searching how the garden's price could reach this—how did it come to this?

sentences.zh: 由吾經始歷年，粗已成立，桃李茂密，桐竹成陰，塍陌交通，渠畎相屬。

translations.literal: Because I began it and passed years, it was roughly established: peach and plum dense and lush, paulownia and bamboo forming shade, field paths connecting, ditches and furrows linked.
translations.idiomatic: Because I began it and passed years, it was roughly established: peach and plum dense and lush, paulownia and bamboo forming shade, field paths connecting, ditches and furrows linked.

sentences.zh: 華樓迥榭，頗有臨眺之美，孤峰叢薄，不無糾紛之興。

translations.literal: Splendid towers and distant pavilions had the beauty of overlooking from afar; solitary peaks and thickets were not without the mood of winding paths.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid towers and distant pavilions had the beauty of overlooking from afar. Solitary peaks and thickets were not without the mood of winding paths.

sentences.zh: 瀆中並饒苻役，湖裏殊富芰蓮。

translations.literal: In the channels there were abundant duckweed duties; in the lake there was especially rich water chestnut and lotus.
translations.idiomatic: In the channels there were abundant duckweed duties; in the lake there was especially rich water chestnut and lotus.

sentences.zh: 雖云人外，城闕密邇，韋生欲之，亦雅有情趣。

translations.literal: Though called beyond human habitation, the city towers were close at hand; Master Wei desired it and also had refined feeling and taste.
translations.idiomatic: Though called beyond human habitation, the city towers were close at hand. Master Wei desired it and also had refined feeling and taste.

sentences.zh: 追述此事，非有吝心，蓋是事意所至爾。

translations.literal: Tracing this matter, there is no stinginess of heart; it is simply where the matter's intent led.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing this matter, there is no stinginess of heart. It is simply where the matter's intent led.

sentences.zh: 憶謝靈運山家詩云：「中為天地物，今成鄙夫有。」

translations.literal: Recalling Xie Lingyun's Mountain Dwelling poem: "Once among Heaven and Earth's things, now possessed by a common man."
translations.idiomatic: Recalling Xie Lingyun's Mountain Dwelling poem: "Once among Heaven and Earth's things, now possessed by a common man."

sentences.zh: 吾此園有之二十載，今為天地物。

translations.literal: I possessed this garden for twenty years; now it is Heaven and Earth's thing.
translations.idiomatic: I possessed this garden for twenty years; now it is Heaven and Earth's thing.

sentences.zh: 物之與我，相校幾何哉。

translations.literal: Things and I—compared, how much difference is there?
translations.idiomatic: Things and I—compared, how much difference is there?

sentences.zh: 此直所餘，今以分汝營小田舍，親累既多，理亦須此。

translations.literal: This is simply what remains; now I divide it for you to manage a small farmstead. Relatives and dependents are many; by reason this is also needed.
translations.idiomatic: This is simply what remains. Now I divide it for you to manage a small farmstead. Relatives and dependents are many; by reason this is also needed.

sentences.zh: 且釋氏之教，以財物謂之外命。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the teaching of the Buddha, wealth and goods are called external life.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the teaching of the Buddha, wealth and goods are called external life.

sentences.zh: 外典亦稱「何以聚人曰財」。

translations.literal: Secular classics also say, "By what are people gathered? By wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Secular classics also say, "By what are people gathered? By wealth."

sentences.zh: 況汝常情，安得忘此。

translations.literal: How much more your ordinary feelings—how can you forget this?
translations.idiomatic: How much more your ordinary feelings—how can you forget this?

sentences.zh: 聞汝所買湖熟田地，甚為舄鹵，彌復可安，所以如此，非物競故也。

translations.literal: I hear the Hushu fields you bought are very saline and brackish, all the more suitable for settling; the reason for this is not competition over things.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Hushu fields you bought are very saline and brackish, all the more suitable for settling. The reason for this is not competition over things.

sentences.zh: 雖事異寢丘，聊可髣佛。

translations.literal: Though the matter differs from the mound of sleep, it can briefly be likened.
translations.idiomatic: Though the matter differs from the mound of sleep, it can briefly be likened.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「居家理事，可移於官。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Managing affairs at home can be transferred to office."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Managing affairs at home can be transferred to office."

sentences.zh: 既已營之，宜使成立，進退兩亡，更貽恥笑。

translations.literal: Since you have already planned it, you should make it succeed; advance and retreat both lost would further bring shame and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Since you have already planned it, you should make it succeed. Advance and retreat both lost would further bring shame and laughter.

sentences.zh: 若有所收穫，汝可自分贍內外大小，宜令得所，非吾所知，又復應沾之諸女爾。

translations.literal: If there is harvest, you may yourself divide support for inner and outer, great and small, making sure each gets what is fitting—not what I know, but also the daughters who should share.
translations.idiomatic: If there is harvest, you may yourself divide support for inner and outer, great and small, making sure each gets what is fitting—not what I know, but also the daughters who should share.

sentences.zh: 汝既居長，故有此及。

translations.literal: Since you occupy the eldest place, therefore there is this extent.
translations.idiomatic: Since you occupy the eldest place, therefore there is this extent.

sentences.zh: 凡為人長，殊復不易，當使中外諧緝，人無間言，先物後己，然後可貴。

translations.literal: For anyone who is eldest, it is especially not easy. One should make inner and outer harmonious and orderly, people without divisive words, things before self—only then is one estimable.
translations.idiomatic: For anyone who is eldest, it is especially not easy. One should make inner and outer harmonious and orderly, people without divisive words, things before self—only then is one estimable.

sentences.zh: 老生云：「後其身而身先。」

translations.literal: The old master said: "Putting oneself last, yet oneself goes first."
translations.idiomatic: The old master said, "Putting oneself last, yet oneself goes first."

sentences.zh: 若能爾者，更招巨利。

translations.literal: If you can be like this, you will further attract great profit.
translations.idiomatic: If you can be like this, you will further attract great profit.

sentences.zh: 汝當自勖，見賢思齊，不宜忽略以棄日也。

translations.literal: You should encourage yourself, seeing the worthy and thinking to equal them; you should not neglect and waste days.
translations.idiomatic: You should encourage yourself, seeing the worthy and thinking to equal them. You should not neglect and waste days.

sentences.zh: 棄日乃是棄身，身名美惡，豈不大哉，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: Wasting days is wasting the person; the beauty or ugliness of person and name—is it not great? Can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Wasting days is wasting the person. The beauty or ugliness of person and name—is it not great? Can one not be cautious!

sentences.zh: 今之所敕，略言此意。

translations.literal: What is admonished now briefly states this intent.
translations.idiomatic: What is admonished now briefly states this intent.

sentences.zh: 政謂為家以來，不事資產，暨立墅舍，似乖舊業，陳其始末，無愧懷抱。

translations.literal: I mean that since managing the household, I have not engaged in assets; then establishing villa residences seems to depart from old practice. Stating the beginning and end, I have no shame in my breast.
translations.idiomatic: I mean that since managing the household, I have not engaged in assets. Then establishing villa residences seems to depart from old practice. Stating the beginning and end, I have no shame in my breast.

sentences.zh: 兼吾年時朽暮，心力稍單，牽課奉公，略不克舉，其中餘暇，裁可自休。

translations.literal: Moreover my years are decayed and twilight, my heart's strength somewhat depleted; dragged by duties serving the public, I can barely manage. The leisure within barely allows self-rest.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my years are decayed and twilight, my heart's strength somewhat depleted. Dragged by duties serving the public, I can barely manage. The leisure within barely allows self-rest.

sentences.zh: 或復冬日之陽，夏日之陰，良辰美景，文案間隟，負杖躡履，逍遙陋館，臨池觀魚，披林聽鳥，濁酒一杯，彈琴一曲，求數刻之暫樂，庶居常以待終，不宜復勞家間細務。

translations.literal: Or again the sun of winter days, the shade of summer days, fine times and beautiful scenes, gaps between documents—leaning on a staff and treading in shoes, roaming freely in a humble lodge, facing the pond to watch fish, parting the woods to listen to birds, a cup of coarse wine, a tune on the zither, seeking a few moments' brief pleasure, hoping to dwell ordinarily awaiting the end—you should not again trouble me with household minutiae.
translations.idiomatic: Or again the sun of winter days, the shade of summer days, fine times and beautiful scenes, gaps between documents—leaning on a staff and treading in shoes, roaming freely in a humble lodge, facing the pond to watch fish, parting the woods to listen to birds, a cup of coarse wine, a tune on the zither, seeking a few moments' brief pleasure, hoping to dwell ordinarily awaiting the end—you should not again trouble me with household minutiae.

sentences.zh: 汝交關既定，此書又行，凡所資須，付給如別。

translations.literal: Your connections are settled, this letter also goes forth; all that is needed for support is delivered as separately listed.
translations.idiomatic: Your connections are settled, this letter also goes forth. All that is needed for support is delivered as separately listed.

sentences.zh: 自茲以後，吾不復言及田事，汝亦勿復與吾言之。

translations.literal: From now on I will not again speak of field affairs; you also must not again speak of them to me.
translations.idiomatic: From now on I will not again speak of field affairs. You also must not again speak of them to me.

sentences.zh: 假使堯水湯旱，豈如之何。

translations.literal: Even if Yao's flood or Tang's drought—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yao's flood or Tang's drought—what then?

sentences.zh: 若其滿庾盈箱，爾之幸遇，如斯之事，並無俟令吾知也。

translations.literal: If granaries are full and boxes overflow, that is your good fortune; matters such as these need not wait for you to inform me.
translations.idiomatic: If granaries are full and boxes overflow, that is your good fortune. Matters such as these need not wait for you to inform me.

sentences.zh: 記云：「夫孝者善繼人之志，善述人之事。」

translations.literal: The Record says: "Filial persons are good at continuing others' intents and good at carrying out others' affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says, "Filial persons are good at continuing others' intents and good at carrying out others' affairs."

sentences.zh: 今且望汝全吾此志，則無所恨矣。

translations.literal: Now I hope you will fulfill this intent of mine; then I will have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hope you will fulfill this intent of mine; then I will have no regret.

sentences.zh: 第二子悱卒，痛悼甚至，不欲久廢王務，乃為答客以自喻焉。

translations.literal: When his second son Fei died, his grief was extreme. Unwilling to long neglect royal duties, he composed a reply to guests to explain himself.
