translations.idiomatic: When his second son Fei died, his grief was extreme. Unwilling to long neglect royal duties, he composed a reply to guests to explain himself.

sentences.zh: 普通末，武帝自算擇後宮吳聲、西曲女妓各一部，並華少，賚勉，因此頗好聲酒。

translations.literal: At the end of Putong, Emperor Wu himself selected from the inner palace one troupe each of Wu-sound and western-melody female performers, all young and splendid, and bestowed them on Mian. Because of this he came to favor music and wine.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Putong, Emperor Wu himself selected from the inner palace one troupe each of Wu-sound and western-melody female performers, all young and splendid, and bestowed them on Mian. Because of this he came to favor music and wine.

sentences.zh: 祿奉之外，月別給錢十萬，信遇之深，故無與匹。

translations.literal: Beyond salary and stipend, each month an additional hundred thousand cash was granted; the depth of trust and favor was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond salary and stipend, each month an additional hundred thousand cash was granted. The depth of trust and favor was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 中大通中，又以疾自陳，移授特進、右光祿大夫、侍中、中衛將軍，置佐史，餘如故。

translations.literal: In Zhongdatong, again pleading illness, he was transferred to Special Advance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Central Guard, with assistant clerks appointed; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong, again pleading illness, he was transferred to Special Advance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Central Guard, with assistant clerks appointed. The rest remained as before.

sentences.zh: 增親信四十人。

translations.literal: Forty trusted attendants were added.
translations.idiomatic: Forty trusted attendants were added.

sentences.zh: 兩宮參問，冠蓋結轍。

translations.literal: Both palaces sent inquiries; carriages and canopies lined the ruts.
translations.idiomatic: Both palaces sent inquiries; carriages and canopies lined the ruts.

sentences.zh: 有敕每欲臨幸，勉以拜伏有虧，頻啟停出，詔許之，遂停輿駕。

translations.literal: There was an edict that each time the emperor wished to visit in person, Mian, because bowing and prostrating would be impaired, repeatedly memorialized to stop the visit; an edict permitted it, and the imperial carriage stopped coming.
translations.idiomatic: There was an edict that each time the emperor wished to visit in person, Mian, because bowing and prostrating would be impaired, repeatedly memorialized to stop the visit. An edict permitted it, and the imperial carriage stopped coming.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝聞而流涕。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor heard and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the emperor heard and wept.

sentences.zh: 即日車駕臨殯，贈右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: That same day the imperial carriage came to the lying in state; he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right and Grand Minister with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the imperial carriage came to the lying in state. He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right and Grand Minister with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 皇太子亦舉哀朝堂。

translations.literal: The crown prince also expressed mourning in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince also expressed mourning in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 有司奏諡「居敬行簡曰簡」，帝益「執心決斷曰肅」，因諡簡肅公。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized the posthumous title "Dwelling in reverence and acting simply, called Jian"; the emperor added "Holding the heart and deciding firmly, called Su," and thus he was posthumously titled Duke Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized the posthumous title "Dwelling in reverence and acting simply, called Jian." The emperor added "Holding the heart and deciding firmly, called Su," and thus he was posthumously titled Duke Jiansu.

sentences.zh: 勉雖骨鯁不及範雲，亦不阿意苟合，後知政事者莫及，梁世之言相者稱范、徐云。

translations.literal: Though Mian's backbone was not equal to Fan Yun's, he also did not flatter and comply rashly. Later those who knew state affairs could not match him. In Liang times those who spoke of chief ministers named Fan and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mian's backbone was not equal to Fan Yun's, he also did not flatter and comply rashly. Later those who knew state affairs could not match him. In Liang times those who spoke of chief ministers named Fan and Xu.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，勤著述，雖當機務，下筆不休。

translations.literal: Skilled at composing prose, diligent in writing, even when handling urgent affairs his brush did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at composing prose and diligent in writing, even when handling urgent affairs his brush did not stop.

sentences.zh: 常以起居注煩雜，乃撰為流別起居注六百六十卷，左丞彈事五卷。

translations.literal: He often found the daily records troublesome and complex, and therefore compiled them into categorized daily records of six hundred sixty scrolls, and five scrolls of impeachments by the Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He often found the daily records troublesome and complex, and therefore compiled them into categorized daily records of six hundred sixty scrolls, and five scrolls of impeachments by the Left Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 在選曹，撰選品三卷。

translations.literal: In the Selection Bureau he compiled three scrolls of Selection Grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the Selection Bureau he compiled three scrolls of Selection Grades.

sentences.zh: 齊時撰太廟祝文二卷。

translations.literal: Under Qi he compiled two scrolls of prayer texts for the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he compiled two scrolls of prayer texts for the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 以孔、釋二教殊途同歸，撰會林五十卷。

translations.literal: Holding that the Confucian and Buddhist teachings differ in path yet converge in return, he compiled the Forest of Convergence in fifty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Holding that the Confucian and Buddhist teachings differ in path yet converge in return, he compiled the Forest of Convergence in fifty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 凡所著前後二集五十卷，又為人章表集十卷。

translations.literal: In all, his earlier and later two collections filled fifty scrolls; he also compiled ten scrolls of memorials for others.
translations.idiomatic: In all, his earlier and later two collections filled fifty scrolls. He also compiled ten scrolls of memorials for others.

sentences.zh: 大同三年，故佐史尚書左丞劉覽等詣闕陳勉行狀，請刊石紀德，即降詔立碑於墓焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, former assistant clerks including Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Liu Lan went to the palace to present Mian's conduct report, requesting stone inscription to record virtue; an edict was immediately issued to erect a stele at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, former assistant clerks including Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Liu Lan went to the palace to present Mian's conduct report, requesting stone inscription to record virtue. An edict was immediately issued to erect a stele at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 悱字敬業，幼聰敏，能屬文，位太子舍人，掌書記。

translations.literal: Fei, styled Jingye, was intelligent from youth and could compose prose. He held the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent and managed records.
translations.idiomatic: Fei, styled Jingye, was intelligent from youth and could compose prose. He served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and managed records.

sentences.zh: 累遷洗馬，中舍人，猶管書記。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Groom and Attendant of the Central Palace, still managing records.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Groom and Attendant of the Central Palace, still managing records.

sentences.zh: 出入宮坊者曆稔。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the palace quarters continued for accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: Entering and leaving the palace quarters continued for many years.

sentences.zh: 以足疾出為湘東王友，俄遷晉安內史。

translations.literal: Because of foot ailment he went out as Friend to the Prince of Xiangdong, and soon was transferred to Administrator of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a foot ailment he went out as Friend to the Prince of Xiangdong, and soon was transferred to Administrator of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 許懋字昭哲，高陽新城人，魏鎮北將軍允九世孫也。

translations.literal: Xu Mao, styled Zhaozhe, was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang, ninth-generation descendant of Yun, General Who Guards the North under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mao, styled Zhaozhe, was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang and a ninth-generation descendant of Yun, General Who Guards the North under Wei.

sentences.zh: 五世祖詢，晉征士。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Xun was a reclusive scholar of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Xun was a reclusive scholar under the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祖珪，宋給事中，著作郎，桂陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was Attendant at Court, Director of Compilation, and Administrator of Guiyang under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui served as Attendant at Court, Director of Compilation, and Administrator of Guiyang under the Song dynasty.

sentences.zh: 父勇慧，齊太子家令，冗從僕射。

translations.literal: His father Yonghui was Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household and Supernumerary Vice Director of Retainers under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yonghui served as Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household and Supernumerary Vice Director of Retainers under the Qi dynasty.

sentences.zh: 懋少孤，性至孝，居父憂執喪過禮。

translations.literal: Mao was orphaned young, supremely filial by nature; in his father's mourning he observed the rites beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was orphaned young and supremely filial by nature. In his father's mourning he observed the rites beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 篤志好學，為州黨所稱。

translations.literal: With steadfast intent he loved learning and was praised by his district and clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: With steadfast intent he loved learning and was praised by his district and clansmen.

sentences.zh: 十四入太學，受毛詩，旦領師說，晚而覆講，坐下聽者常數十百人，因撰風雅比興義十五卷，盛行于時。

translations.literal: At fourteen he entered the Imperial University and studied the Mao version of the Book of Songs. In the morning he received the master's teaching; in the evening he lectured in return. Listeners seated below often numbered in the tens and hundreds. He therefore compiled fifteen scrolls on the meaning of the Airs, Elegantiae, and comparison-and-arousal, which flourished at the time.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered the Imperial University and studied the Mao version of the Book of Songs. In the morning he received the master's teaching; in the evening he lectured in return. Listeners seated below often numbered in the tens and hundreds. He therefore compiled fifteen scrolls on the meaning of the Airs, Elegantiae, and comparison-and-arousal, which flourished at the time.

sentences.zh: 尤明故事，稱為儀注學。

translations.literal: He was especially clear on precedents and was called a scholar of ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially clear on precedents and was called a scholar of ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 起家後軍豫章王行參軍，轉法曹。

translations.literal: He began his career as Acting Military Affairs Aide to the Rear Army under Prince Yuzhang, then transferred to the Legal Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Acting Military Affairs Aide to the Rear Army under Prince Yuzhang, then transferred to the Legal Bureau.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，遷驃騎大將軍儀同中記室。

translations.literal: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he was transferred to Records Officer in the Secretariat of the General of Agile Cavalry with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he was transferred to Records Officer in the Secretariat of the General of Agile Cavalry with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子聞而召之，侍講於崇明殿。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhuì heard of him and summoned him to lecture at Chongming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhuì heard of him and summoned him to lecture at Chongming Hall.

sentences.zh: 後兼國子博士，與司馬褧同志友善。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as erudite of the National University and was of one intent and friendly with Sima Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he concurrently served as erudite of the National University and was of one intent and friendly with Sima Jiong.

sentences.zh: 僕射江祏甚推重之，號為經史笥。

translations.literal: Vice Director Jiang Si greatly esteemed him and called him a basket of classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Jiang Si greatly esteemed him and called him a basket of classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，吏部尚書范雲舉懋參詳五禮，除征西鄱陽王諮議參軍，兼著作郎，待詔文德省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, Minister of the Personnel Bureau Fan Yun recommended Mao to examine the Five Rites in detail. He was appointed Military Affairs Counselor to the Campaign West under Prince Poyang, concurrently Director of Compilation, awaiting edicts at the Wende Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, Minister of the Personnel Bureau Fan Yun recommended Mao to examine the Five Rites in detail. He was appointed Military Affairs Counselor to the Campaign West under Prince Poyang, concurrently Director of Compilation, awaiting edicts at the Wende Office.

sentences.zh: 時有請會稽封禪者，武帝因集儒學士草封禪儀，將行焉，懋建議獨以為不可。

translations.literal: At the time someone requested a feng and shan ceremony at Kuaiji. Emperor Wu therefore gathered Confucian scholars to draft the feng and shan rites and was about to proceed. Mao alone memorialized that it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone requested a feng and shan ceremony at Kuaiji. Emperor Wu therefore gathered Confucian scholars to draft the feng and shan rites and was about to proceed. Mao alone memorialized that it was not permissible.

sentences.zh: 帝見其議，嘉納之，由是遂停。

translations.literal: The emperor saw his proposal, praised and accepted it, and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his proposal, praised and accepted it, and therefore stopped.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉太子家令。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 凡諸禮儀，多所刊正。

translations.literal: Among all ritual proprieties he corrected many.
translations.idiomatic: Among all ritual proprieties he corrected many.

sentences.zh: 以足疾，出為始平太守，政有能名，加散騎常侍，轉天門太守。

translations.literal: Because of foot ailment he went out as Administrator of Shiping; his governance had a reputation for ability. He was additionally granted Regular Attendant and transferred to Administrator of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a foot ailment he went out as Administrator of Shiping; his governance had a reputation for ability. He was additionally granted Regular Attendant and transferred to Administrator of Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，皇太子召與諸儒錄長春義記。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong, the crown prince summoned him with various Confucians to record the Changchun Exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongdatong, the crown prince summoned him with various Confucians to record the Changchun Exegesis.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜中庶子。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 是歲卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 撰述行記四卷，有集十五卷。

translations.literal: He compiled a Conduct Record in four scrolls and had a collected works of fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a Conduct Record in four scrolls and had a collected works of fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子亨。

translations.literal: His son was Heng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Heng.

sentences.zh: 亨字亨道，少傳家業，孤介有節行。

translations.literal: Heng, styled Hengdao, from youth inherited the family profession, solitary and upright with integrity of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, styled Hengdao, from youth inherited the family profession. Solitary and upright, he had integrity of conduct.

sentences.zh: 博通群書，多識前代舊事，甚為南陽劉之遴所重。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in all books, he knew much of earlier generations' old affairs and was greatly esteemed by Liu Zhilin of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly versed in all books, he knew much of earlier generations' old affairs and was greatly esteemed by Liu Zhilin of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 梁太清初，為西中郎記室，兼太常丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing under Liang, he served as Records Officer of the Western Palace Guard and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiqing under Liang, he served as Records Officer of the Western Palace Guard and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，避地郢州。

translations.literal: During the Hou Jing rebellion he fled to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hou Jing rebellion he fled to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會梁邵陵王自東至，引為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Shaoling of Liang came from the east, he recruited him as Military Affairs Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shaoling of Liang came from the east, he recruited him as Military Affairs Counselor.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯之襲郢州，素聞其名，召為儀同從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian attacked Yingzhou, having long heard his name, he summoned him as Attendant of Affairs with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian attacked Yingzhou, having long heard his name, he summoned him as Attendant of Affairs with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉從事中郎，與吳興沈炯對掌書記，府政朝務，一以委之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of Affairs to the Grand Commandant and, with Shen Jiong of Wuxing, jointly managed records; prefectural governance and court affairs were all entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant of Affairs to the Grand Commandant and, with Shen Jiong of Wuxing, jointly managed records. Prefectural governance and court affairs were all entrusted to them.

sentences.zh: 晉安王承制，授給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Prince Jin'an by provisional order granted him Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin'an by provisional order granted him Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，為太中大夫，領大著作，知梁史事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen accepted the abdication, he became Grand Master for All-Purpose, concurrently overseeing the Grand Compilation and managing affairs of Liang history.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen accepted the abdication, he became Grand Master for All-Purpose, concurrently overseeing the Grand Compilation and managing affairs of Liang history.

sentences.zh: 初僧辯之誅也，所司收僧辯及其子頠屍，于方山同坎埋瘞，至是無敢言者，亨以故吏抗表請葬之。

translations.literal: When Sengbian was executed, the relevant offices collected Sengbian and his son Yi's corpses and buried them in one pit at Fang Mountain. At this time none dared speak of it. Heng, as a former subordinate, submitted a bold memorial requesting burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian was executed, the relevant offices collected Sengbian and his son Yi's corpses and buried them in one pit at Fang Mountain. At this time none dared speak of it. Heng, as a former subordinate, submitted a bold memorial requesting burial.

sentences.zh: 與故義徐陵、張種、孔奐等相率以家財營葬，凡七柩，皆改窆焉。

translations.literal: Together with former righteous companions Xu Ling, Zhang Zhong, Kong Huan, and others, he led the way in using family wealth to arrange burial; in all seven coffins were reinterred.
translations.idiomatic: Together with former righteous companions Xu Ling, Zhang Zhong, Kong Huan, and others, he led the way in using family wealth to arrange burial. In all seven coffins were reinterred.

sentences.zh: 光大中，宣帝入輔，以亨貞正有古人風，甚相欽重，常以師禮事之。

translations.literal: During Guangda, Emperor Xuan entered to assist the government; because Heng was upright and correct and had the manner of men of antiquity, he greatly honored and respected him, and constantly served him with the rites due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangda, Emperor Xuan entered to assist the government. Because Heng was upright and correct and had the manner of men of antiquity, he greatly honored and respected him, and constantly treated him with the rites due a teacher.

sentences.zh: 及到仲舉之謀出宣帝，宣帝問亨，亨勸勿奉詔。

translations.literal: When Dao Zhongju plotted to send Emperor Xuan out, Emperor Xuan asked Heng, and Heng advised him not to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao Zhongju plotted to send Emperor Xuan out, Emperor Xuan asked Heng, and Heng advised him not to obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，拜衛尉卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Heng was appointed Chamberlain for the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Heng was appointed Chamberlain for the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 亨初撰齊書並志五十卷，遇亂亡失。

translations.literal: Heng at first compiled the Book of Qi and its annals in fifty scrolls; encountering chaos they were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Heng at first compiled the Book of Qi and its annals in fifty scrolls, but they were lost in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 後撰梁史，成者五十八卷。

translations.literal: Later he compiled the History of Liang; what was completed filled fifty-eight scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Later he compiled the History of Liang; what was completed filled fifty-eight scrolls.

sentences.zh: 梁太清之後，所制文筆六卷。

translations.literal: After Taiqing under Liang, his literary writings filled six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiqing under Liang, his literary writings filled six scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子善心，位尚書度支侍郎。

translations.literal: His son was Shanxin, who held the post of Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shanxin served as Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 殷鈞字季和，陳郡長平人，晉荊州刺史仲堪五世孫也。

translations.literal: Yin Jun, styled Jihe, was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery, fifth-generation descendant of Zhongkan, Governor of Jingzhou under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jun, styled Jihe, was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery and a fifth-generation descendant of Zhongkan, Governor of Jingzhou under the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 曾祖元素，宋南康相，坐元凶事誅。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuansu was Chancellor of Nankang under Song and was executed for involvement in the Crown Prince's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuansu served as Chancellor of Nankang under the Song dynasty and was executed for involvement in the Crown Prince's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 元素娶尚書僕射琅邪王僧朗女，生子寧早卒，寧遺腹生子叡，亦當從戮，僧朗啟孝武救之得免。

translations.literal: Yuansu married the daughter of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Senglang of Langya and had a son Ning who died early. Ning's posthumous son was Rui, who was also to be executed along with him. Senglang memorialized Emperor Xiaowu to save him and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu married the daughter of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Senglang of Langya and had a son Ning who died early. Ning's posthumous son was Rui, who was also to be executed along with him. Senglang memorialized Emperor Xiaowu to save him, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 叡有口辯，司徒褚彥回甚重之，謂曰：「諸殷自荊州以來無出卿。」

translations.literal: Rui had eloquence in debate. Minister of Works Chu Yanhui greatly valued him and said: "Among all the Yin clan since Jingzhou, none surpasses you."
translations.idiomatic: Rui was eloquent in debate. Minister of Works Chu Yanhui greatly valued him and said, "Among all the Yin clan since Jingzhou, none surpasses you."

sentences.zh: 叡斂容答曰：「殷族衰悴，誠不如昔，若此旨為虛，故不足降，此旨為實，彌不可聞。」

translations.literal: Rui composed his expression and answered: "The Yin clan is decayed and withered, truly not as in the past. If this intent is empty, it is therefore not worth lowering oneself to; if this intent is real, all the more it must not be heard."
translations.idiomatic: Rui composed his expression and answered, "The Yin clan is decayed and withered, truly not as in the past. If this intent is empty, it is therefore not worth lowering oneself to. If this intent is real, all the more it must not be heard."

sentences.zh: 仕齊曆司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He served Qi and successively held the post of Attendant of Affairs to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Qi and successively held the post of Attendant of Affairs to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 叡妻琅邪王奐女，奐為雍州刺史，啟叡為府長史。

translations.literal: Rui's wife was the daughter of Wang Huan of Langya. Huan was Governor of Yongzhou and recommended Rui as chief clerk of the princely administration.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's wife was the daughter of Wang Huan of Langya. Huan was Governor of Yongzhou and recommended Rui as chief clerk of the princely administration.

sentences.zh: 奐誅，叡亦見害。

translations.literal: When Huan was executed, Rui was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan was executed, Rui was also killed.

sentences.zh: 鈞九歲以孝聞，及長，恬靜簡交遊，好學有思理，善隸書，為當時楷法。

translations.literal: Jun at nine was known for filial piety. When grown he was tranquil and quiet, simplifying social contacts, loving learning with thoughtful principle, skilled at clerical script, and was the model standard of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Jun at nine was known for filial piety. When grown he was tranquil and quiet, simplifying social contacts, loving learning with thoughtful principle, skilled at clerical script, and was the model standard of the time.

sentences.zh: 南鄉范雲、樂安任昉並稱美之。

translations.literal: Fan Yun of Nanxiang and Ren Fang of Le'an both praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun of Nanxiang and Ren Fang of Le'an both praised him.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝與叡少故舊，以女永興公主妻鈞，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang and Rui were old friends from youth; he gave his daughter Princess Yongxing in marriage to Jun and appointed him Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang and Rui were old friends from youth. He gave his daughter Princess Yongxing in marriage to Jun and appointed him Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 曆秘書丞，在職啟校定秘閣四部書，更為目錄。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director of the Secretariat and, while in office, memorialized to collate and fix the four divisions of books in the Secret Archive and make a new catalog.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Director of the Secretariat and, while in office, memorialized to collate and fix the four divisions of books in the Secret Archive and make a new catalog.

sentences.zh: 又受詔料檢西省法書古跡，列為品目。

translations.literal: He also received an edict to examine and inspect ancient traces of model calligraphy in the Western Office and arrange them into grades and categories.
translations.idiomatic: He also received an edict to examine and inspect ancient traces of model calligraphy in the Western Office and arrange them into grades and categories.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中，東宮學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and scholar of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and scholar of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 自宋、齊以來，公主多驕淫無行，永興主加以險虐。

translations.literal: From Song and Qi onward, princesses were mostly arrogant, licentious, and without proper conduct; the Princess of Yongxing added to this cruelty and tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: From Song and Qi onward, princesses were mostly arrogant, licentious, and without proper conduct. The Princess of Yongxing added to this cruelty and tyranny.

sentences.zh: 鈞形貌短小，為主所憎，每被召入，先滿壁為殷叡字，鈞輒流涕以出，主命婢束而反之。

translations.literal: Jun's appearance was short and small; he was hated by the princess. Each time he was summoned in, the walls were first filled with the characters for Yin Rui. Jun would weep as he left; the princess ordered maids to bind him and send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's appearance was short and small, and he was hated by the princess. Each time he was summoned in, the walls were first filled with the characters for Yin Rui. Jun would weep as he left, and the princess ordered maids to bind him and send him back.

sentences.zh: 鈞不勝怒而言於帝，帝以犀如意擊主碎於背，然猶恨鈞。

translations.literal: Jun, unable to bear his anger, spoke to the emperor. The emperor struck the princess's back with a rhinoceros-horn ruyi scepter and broke it, yet still resented Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, unable to bear his anger, spoke to the emperor. The emperor struck the princess's back with a rhinoceros-horn ruyi scepter and broke it, yet still resented Jun.

sentences.zh: 自侍中出為王府諮議，後為明威將軍、臨川內史。

translations.literal: From Attendant-in-Ordinary he went out as Military Affairs Counselor to a princely administration, later becoming General of Bright Might and Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: From Attendant-in-Ordinary he went out as Military Affairs Counselor to a princely administration, later becoming General of Bright Might and Administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 鈞體羸多疾，閉合臥理，而百姓化其德，劫盜皆奔出境。

translations.literal: Jun's body was frail and often ill; he shut his doors and administered affairs from bed, yet the common people were transformed by his virtue and bandits and robbers all fled beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's body was frail and often ill. He shut his doors and administered affairs from bed, yet the common people were transformed by his virtue and bandits and robbers all fled beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 嘗禽劫帥，不加考掠，和言誚責。

translations.literal: Once he captured a bandit chief and did not apply torture, but with gentle words reproached and blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he captured a bandit chief and did not apply torture, but with gentle words reproached and blamed him.

sentences.zh: 劫帥稽顙乞改過，鈞便命遣之，後遂為善人。

translations.literal: The bandit chief kowtowed and begged to reform; Jun then ordered him released, and afterward he became a good man.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chief kowtowed and begged to reform. Jun then ordered him released, and afterward he became a good man.

sentences.zh: 郡舊多山瘧，更暑必動，自鈞在任，郡境無復瘧疾。

translations.literal: The commandery formerly had much mountain malaria that always flared in summer; from the time Jun held office, within the commandery there was no longer malarial illness.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery formerly had much mountain malaria that always flared in summer. From the time Jun held office, within the commandery there was no longer malarial illness.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，居喪過禮，昭明太子憂之，手書誡喻。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office and observed mourning beyond the rites. Crown Prince Zhaoming was concerned and wrote a personal letter admonishing and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death he left office and observed mourning beyond the rites. Crown Prince Zhaoming was concerned and wrote a personal letter admonishing and instructing him.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為散騎常侍，領步兵校尉，侍東宮。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Regular Attendant, concurrently Commandant of Footsoldiers, attending the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became Regular Attendant, concurrently Commandant of Footsoldiers, attending the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 改領中庶子，後為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was changed to concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, later becoming Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, later becoming Chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡貞。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was given the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 二子構、渥。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Gou and Wo.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Gou and Wo.

sentences.zh: 鈞宗人芸。

translations.literal: Jun's clansman was Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's clansman was Yun.

sentences.zh: 芸字灌蔬，倜儻不拘細行，然不妄交遊，門無雜客。

translations.literal: Yun, styled Guanshu, was unrestrained and not bound by minor conduct, yet he did not socialize rashly and had no miscellaneous guests at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, styled Guanshu, was unrestrained and not bound by minor conduct, yet he did not socialize rashly and had no miscellaneous guests at his gate.

sentences.zh: 勵精勤學，博洽群書。

translations.literal: He exerted his spirit and studied diligently, broadly mastering all books.
translations.idiomatic: He exerted his spirit and studied diligently, broadly mastering all books.

sentences.zh: 幼而廬江何憲見之，深相歎賞。

translations.literal: In youth He Xian of Lujiang saw him and deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In youth He Xian of Lujiang saw him and deeply sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 天監中，位秘書監、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era he held the posts of Director of the Palace Library and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjian era he held the posts of Director of the Palace Library and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 後直東宮學士省，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served in the Eastern Palace Scholars Office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served in the Eastern Palace Scholars Office and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：範懋賓之德美，傅茂遠之清令，孔休源之政事，江休映之強直，並加之以學植，飾之以文采，其所以取高時主，豈徒然哉。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The virtue and beauty of Fan Maobin, the clarity and excellence of Fu Maoyuan, the governance of Kong Xiuyuan, the forceful uprightness of Jiang Xiuying—all further enhanced by learning and cultivation, adorned by literary grace—the reason they won high regard from the sovereigns of their age was surely not for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The virtue and beauty of Fan Maobin, the clarity and excellence of Fu Maoyuan, the governance of Kong Xiuyuan, the forceful uprightness of Jiang Xiuying—all further enhanced by learning and cultivation, adorned by literary grace—the reason they won high regard from the sovereigns of their age was surely not for nothing.

sentences.zh: 徐勉少而勵志，發憤忘食，修身慎行，運屬興王，依光日月，致位公輔，提衡端執，時無異議，為梁氏宗臣，信為美矣。

translations.literal: Xu Mian from youth encouraged his will, striving in anger and forgetting food, cultivating himself and acting with caution. His fortune belonged to the rising king; relying on the light of sun and moon, he reached the rank of chief minister, holding the scales upright—at the time there was no dissent. As a pillar minister of the Liang house, he was truly admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian from youth encouraged his will, striving in anger and forgetting food, cultivating himself and acting with caution. His fortune belonged to the rising king. Relying on the light of sun and moon, he reached the rank of chief minister, holding the scales upright—at the time there was no dissent. As a pillar minister of the Liang house, he was truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 許懋業藝，以經笥見推，亨懷道好古，以博覽歸譽，其所以折議封禪，求葬僧辯，正直存焉，豈唯文義而已。

translations.literal: Xu Mao's professional arts were praised as a basket of classics; Heng cherished the Way and loved antiquity, winning reputation for broad reading. The reason they argued against the feng and shan ceremony and sought burial for Sengbian—uprightness was preserved there; was it only literary meaning?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mao's professional arts were praised as a basket of classics. Heng cherished the Way and loved antiquity, winning reputation for broad reading. The reason they argued against the feng and shan ceremony and sought burial for Sengbian—uprightness was preserved there. Was it only literary meaning?

sentences.zh: 古人云：「仁者有勇」，斯言近之。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "The benevolent have courage." This saying comes close.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "The benevolent have courage." This saying comes close.

sentences.zh: 殷鈞德業自居，又加之以政績，文質斌斌，亦足稱也。

translations.literal: Yin Jun rested in virtue and achievement, further enhanced by administrative results; substance and pattern balanced and splendid—he too is worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jun rested in virtue and achievement, further enhanced by administrative results. Substance and pattern balanced and splendid—he too is worth praise.
